12.4.89.s: athainān sruvāhutibhir abhijuhoti | agnaye rakṣoghne svāhā | iti pañcabhis |
12.4.89.d: अथैनान् स्रुवाहुतिभिर् अभिजुहोति । अग्नये रक्षोघ्ने स्वाहा । इति पञ्चभिस् ।
12.4.89.m: Then he makes libations over them with ladle libations, with five [recitations of]: 'To Agni, slayer of rakṣases, svāhā!'

12.4.89.s: atra praṣṭivāhinam̐ rathaṃ dadāti | atha yācati parṇamayam̐ sruvam apāmārgasaktūn prativasanīyaṃ vāso 'ntam āgārād ekolmukam udapātram iti |
12.4.89.d: अत्र प्रष्टिवाहिनँ रथं ददाति । अथ याचति पर्णमयँ स्रुवम् अपामार्गसक्तून् प्रतिवसनीयं वासो ऽन्तम् आगाराद् एकोल्मुकम् उदपात्रम् इति ।
12.4.89.m: Here he gives a chariot drawn by three horses. Then he asks for a parṇa-wood ladle, groats of apāmārga seeds, a garment to change into from the inside of the house, a single firebrand, [and] a vessel of water.

12.4.89.s: etat samādāyodañco niṣkramya tāṃ diśaṃ yanti yatrāsya svakṛtamiriṇam̐ spaṣṭaṃ bhavati pradaro vā
12.4.89.d: एतत् समादायोदञ्चो निष्क्रम्य तां दिशं यन्ति यत्रास्य स्वकृतमिरिणँ स्पष्टं भवति प्रदरो वा
12.4.89.m: Taking these and stepping out toward the north, they go in that direction where there is an evident natural cleft or fissure.

12.4.89.s: tad etad ekolmukam upasamādhāya saṃparistīrya parṇamayena sruveṇāpāmārgasaktūñ juhoti devasya tvā savituḥ prasave 'śvinor bāhubhyāṃ pūṣṇo hastābhyām̐ rakṣaso vadhaṃ juhomi svāhā | iti
12.4.89.d: तद् एतद् एकोल्मुकम् उपसमाधाय संपरिस्तीर्य पर्णमयेन स्रुवेणापामार्गसक्तूञ् जुहोति देवस्य त्वा सवितुः प्रसवे ऽश्विनोर् बाहुभ्यां पूष्णो हस्ताभ्याँ रक्षसो वधं जुहोमि स्वाहा । इति
12.4.89.m: Having added fuel to this single firebrand and spread grass around it, he offers the apāmārga groats with the parṇa-wood ladle [with the mantra]: 'At the impulse of god Savitar, with the arms of the Aśvins, with the hands of Pūṣan, I offer the weapon against the rakṣas, svāhā!'
With the words: 'Slain is the rakṣas!', he casts the ladle into the fire.

12.4.89.s: avadhiṣma rakṣas | ity upatiṣṭhate | atra yad vaste tad dadāti |
12.4.89.d: अवधिष्म रक्षस् । इत्य् उपतिष्ठते । अत्र यद् वस्ते तद् ददाति ।
12.4.89.m: He worships [the fire] with the words: 'We have slain the rakṣas!' Here he gives what he is wearing.

12.4.89.s: athāpo vyatiṣicya parāsya pātram anavekṣmāṇā āyanti hastapādān prakṣālya |
12.4.89.d: अथापो व्यतिषिच्य परास्य पात्रम् अनवेक्ष्माणा आयन्ति हस्तपादान् प्रक्षाल्य ।
12.4.89.m: Then, having poured out water and thrown away the vessel, they return without looking back, having washed their hands and feet.

12.4.89.s: etena yathetam etyendraturīyeṇa sam̐sthāṃ karoti | atha navame 'hni pūrvāṇi devikāhavīm̐ṣi nirvapaty anumatyai carum̐ rākāyai caruṃ dhātre puroḍāśaṃ dvādaśakapālam iti |
12.4.89.d: एतेन यथेतम् एत्येन्द्रतुरीयेण सँस्थां करोति । अथ नवमे ऽह्नि पूर्वाणि देविकाहवीँषि निर्वपत्य् अनुमत्यै चरुँ राकायै चरुं धात्रे पुरोडाशं द्वादशकपालम् इति ।
12.4.89.m: Having returned by the same way they came, he concludes [the rite] with the Indraturīya. Then on the ninth day he measures out the earlier Devikā oblations: a caru for Anumati, a caru for Rākā, and a cake on twelve potsherds for Dhātṛ.
Having placed the anvāhārya cooked rice, he gives a heifer.

12.4.90.s: atha daśame 'hny uttarāṇi devikāhavīm̐ṣi nirvapati sinīvālyai caruṃ kuhvai caruṃ dhātra eva puroḍāśaṃ dvādaśakapālam iti |
12.4.90.d: अथ दशमे ऽह्न्य् उत्तराणि देविकाहवीँषि निर्वपति सिनीवाल्यै चरुं कुह्वै चरुं धात्र एव पुरोडाशं द्वादशकपालम् इति ।
12.4.90.m: Then on the tenth day he measures out the later Devikā oblations: a caru for Sinīvālī, a caru for Kuhū, and a cake on twelve potsherds for Dhātṛ alone.
Having placed the anvāhārya cooked rice, he gives a young bull.

12.4.90.s: athaikādaśe 'hni triṣaṃyuktaiḥ pratipadyata āgnāvaiṣṇavaṃ nirvapaty aindrāvaiṣṇavam ekādaśakapālaṃ vaiṣṇavaṃ trikapālam |
12.4.90.d: अथैकादशे ऽह्नि त्रिषंयुक्तैः प्रतिपद्यत आग्नावैष्णवं निर्वपत्य् ऐन्द्रावैष्णवम् एकादशकपालं वैष्णवं त्रिकपालम् ।
12.4.90.m: Then on the eleventh day he begins with the triple offerings: he measures out [a cake] for Agni and Viṣṇu, [a cake] on eleven potsherds for Indra and Viṣṇu, [and] a cake on three potsherds for Viṣṇu.
He gives a dwarf draught bull.

12.4.90.s: atha dvādaśe 'hny agnīṣomīyam ekādaśakapālaṃ nirvapatīndrāsomīyam ekādaśakapālam̐ saumyaṃ carum |
12.4.90.d: अथ द्वादशे ऽह्न्य् अग्नीषोमीयम् एकादशकपालं निर्वपतीन्द्रासोमीयम् एकादशकपालँ सौम्यं चरुम् ।
12.4.90.m: Then on the twelfth day he measures out a cake on eleven potsherds for Agni and Soma, a cake on eleven potsherds for Indra and Soma, and a caru for Soma.

12.4.90.s: babhruṃ dadāti | atha trayodaśe 'hni somāpauṣṇaṃ caruṃ nirvapaty aindrāpauṣṇaṃ caruṃ pauṣṇaṃ carum |
12.4.90.d: बभ्रुं ददाति । अथ त्रयोदशे ऽह्नि सोमापौष्णं चरुं निर्वपत्य् ऐन्द्रापौष्णं चरुं पौष्णं चरुम् ।
12.4.90.m: He gives a brown [bull]. Then, on the thirteenth day, he prepares an offering of a mess of cooked grain for Soma and Pūṣan, a mess of cooked grain for Indra and Pūṣan, [and] a mess of cooked grain for Pūṣan.

12.4.90.s: śyāmaṃ dadāti | atha caturdaśe 'hni vaiśvānaraṃ dvādaśakapālaṃ nirvapati
12.4.90.d: श्यामं ददाति । अथ चतुर्दशे ऽह्नि वैश्वानरं द्वादशकपालं निर्वपति
12.4.90.m: He gives a dark-grey [bull]. Then, on the fourteenth day, he prepares an offering of a cake on twelve potsherds for Vaiśvānara.

12.4.90.s: hiraṇyaṃ dadāti | atha pañcadaśe 'hni vāruṇaṃ yavamayaṃ carum
12.4.90.d: हिरण्यं ददाति । अथ पञ्चदशे ऽह्नि वारुणं यवमयं चरुम्
12.4.90.m: He gives gold. Then, on the fifteenth day, [he prepares an offering of] a mess of cooked barley grain for Varuṇa.

12.5.90.s: athainam āmāvāsyena haviṣejānam̐ ratninaḥ paryavasyanti dakṣiṇato vodañco paścād vā prāñcas
12.5.90.d: अथैनम् आमावास्येन हविषेजानँ रत्निनः पर्यवस्यन्ति दक्षिणतो वोदञ्चो पश्चाद् वा प्राञ्चस्
12.5.90.m: Now, when he has sacrificed with the new-moon oblation, the royal dignitaries take up quarters around him, either to the south facing north, or to the west facing east.

12.5.90.s: teṣām avasitānāṃ brahmaiva dakṣiṇārdhyo vāparārdhyo vā bhavati
12.5.90.d: तेषाम् अवसितानां ब्रह्मैव दक्षिणार्ध्यो वापरार्ध्यो वा भवति
12.5.90.m: Of those who have taken up quarters, the brahman priest is either on the southern side or on the western side.

12.5.90.s: sa yat kiṃca yajñaparibhojanaṃ brahmaṇa eva tad gṛhe bhavati |
12.5.90.d: स यत् किंच यज्ञपरिभोजनं ब्रह्मण एव तद् गृहे भवति ।
12.5.90.m: Whatever [utensil is meant] for use during the sacrifice is indeed in the house of the brahman priest.

12.5.90.s: athāraṇyor agnīn samārohya brahmaṇo gṛhān adhyavasāya mathitvāgnīn vihṛtya bārhaspatyaṃ caruṃ nirvapati brahmaṇo gṛhe
12.5.90.d: अथारण्योर् अग्नीन् समारोह्य ब्रह्मणो गृहान् अध्यवसाय मथित्वाग्नीन् विहृत्य बार्हस्पत्यं चरुं निर्वपति ब्रह्मणो गृहे
12.5.90.m: Then, having mounted the fires into the churning-sticks, having approached the house of the brahman priest, having churned [the fire], and having spread the fires, he prepares an offering of a mess of cooked grain for Bṛhaspati in the house of the brahman priest.

12.5.91.s: śitipṛṣṭhaṃ dadāti | athāraṇyor agnīn samārohya svāny agnyāyatanāny abhipravrajati
12.5.91.d: शितिपृष्ठं ददाति । अथारण्योर् अग्नीन् समारोह्य स्वान्य् अग्न्यायतनान्य् अभिप्रव्रजति
12.5.91.m: He gives a white-backed [bull]. Then, having mounted the fires into the churning-sticks, he proceeds towards his own fire-places.

12.5.91.s: taṃ yantam anumantrayate | ayaṃ no rājā vṛtrahā rājā bhūtvā vṛtraṃ vadhyāt | iti |
12.5.91.d: तं यन्तम् अनुमन्त्रयते । अयं नो राजा वृत्रहा राजा भूत्वा वृत्रं वध्यात् । इति ।
12.5.91.m: He accompanies him as he goes with the mantra: 'May this king of ours, slayer of Vṛtra, having become king, slay Vṛtra!'

12.5.91.s: atha svāny agnyāyatanāny adhyavasāya mathitvāgnīn vihṛtyendrāya sutrāmṇe puroḍāśam ekādaśakapālaṃ pratinirvapati |
12.5.91.d: अथ स्वान्य् अग्न्यायतनान्य् अध्यवसाय मथित्वाग्नीन् विहृत्येन्द्राय सुत्राम्णे पुरोडाशम् एकादशकपालं प्रतिनिर्वपति ।
12.5.91.m: Then, having approached his own fire-places, having churned [the fire], and having spread the fires, he offers in return a cake on eleven potsherds for Indra Sutrāman.

12.5.91.s: athāsyaitad ahaḥ śvetāyai śvetavatsāyai payo dohayitvā samātacya nidadhāti |
12.5.91.d: अथास्यैतद् अहः श्वेतायै श्वेतवत्सायै पयो दोहयित्वा समातच्य निदधाति ।
12.5.91.m: Then, on this day, having milked the milk of a white cow with a white calf, [and] having curdled it, he sets it aside.

12.5.91.s: atha śvo bhūte 'raṇyor agnīn samārohya rājanyasya gṛhān adhyavasāya mathitvāgnīn vihṛtyaindram ekādaśakapālam̐ rājanyasya gṛhe |
12.5.91.d: अथ श्वो भूते ऽरण्योर् अग्नीन् समारोह्य राजन्यस्य गृहान् अध्यवसाय मथित्वाग्नीन् विहृत्यैन्द्रम् एकादशकपालँ राजन्यस्य गृहे ।
12.5.91.m: Then, on the next day, having mounted the fires into the churning-sticks, having approached the house of the rājanya, having churned [the fire], and having spread the fires, [he offers a cake] on eleven potsherds for Indra in the house of the rājanya.

12.5.91.s: ṛṣabhaṃ dadāti tathāraṇyor agnīn samārohya svāny evāgnyāyatanāny abhipravrajati
12.5.91.d: ऋषभं ददाति तथारण्योर् अग्नीन् समारोह्य स्वान्य् एवाग्न्यायतनान्य् अभिप्रव्रजति
12.5.91.m: He gives a bull. In the same way, having mounted the fires into the churning-sticks, he proceeds towards his own fire-places.
He accompanies him in the very same way as he goes.

12.5.91.s: yasyayasya gṛhe yajate saso 'numantrayate | ayaṃ no rājā vṛtrahā rājā hūtvā vṛtraṃ vadhyāt | iti |
12.5.91.d: यस्ययस्य गृहे यजते ससो ऽनुमन्त्रयते । अयं नो राजा वृत्रहा राजा हूत्वा वृत्रं वध्यात् । इति ।
12.5.91.m: In whose house he sacrifices, that one accompanies him [with the formula]: 'May this king of ours, slayer of Vṛtra, having become king, slay Vṛtra!'

12.5.91.s: atha svāny evānyāyatanāny adhyavasāya mathitvāgnīn vihṛtyendrāyām̐homuce puroḍāśam ekādaśakapālaṃ pratinirvapati
12.5.91.d: अथ स्वान्य् एवान्यायतनान्य् अध्यवसाय मथित्वाग्नीन् विहृत्येन्द्रायाँहोमुचे पुरोडाशम् एकादशकपालं प्रतिनिर्वपति
12.5.91.m: Then, having approached his own fire-places, having churned [the fire], and having spread the fires, he offers in return a cake on eleven potsherds for Indra Aṃhomuc.

12.5.91.s: prajātam evāsyaitad ahaḥ śvetāyai śvetavatsāyai payo dohayitvā samātacyaiva nidadhāti |
12.5.91.d: प्रजातम् एवास्यैतद् अहः श्वेतायै श्वेतवत्सायै पयो दोहयित्वा समातच्यैव निदधाति ।
12.5.91.m: In the very same manner, on this day, having milked the milk of a white cow with a white calf, [and] having curdled it, he sets it aside.

12.5.91.s: atha tṛtīye 'hny ādityaṃ caruṃ mahiṣyai gṛhe
12.5.91.d: अथ तृतीये ऽह्न्य् आदित्यं चरुं महिष्यै गृहे
12.5.91.m: Then, on the third day, [he offers] a mess of cooked grain for Aditi in the house of the chief queen.

12.5.91.s: dhenuṃ dadāti | atha caturthe 'hni bhagāya caruṃ vāvātāyai gṛhe
12.5.91.d: धेनुं ददाति । अथ चतुर्थे ऽह्नि भगाय चरुं वावातायै गृहे
12.5.91.m: He gives a milch cow. Then, on the fourth day, [he offers] a mess of cooked grain for Bhaga in the house of the favourite wife.

12.5.91.s: vicittagarbhāṃ paṣṭhaihīṃ dadāti | atha pañcame 'hni nairṛtaṃ caruṃ parivṛktyai gṛhe kṛṣṇānāṃ vrīhīṇāṃ nakhanirbhinnam |
12.5.91.d: विचित्तगर्भां पष्ठैहीं ददाति । अथ पञ्चमे ऽह्नि नैरृतं चरुं परिवृक्त्यै गृहे कृष्णानां व्रीहीणां नखनिर्भिन्नम् ।
12.5.91.m: He gives a six-year-old cow whose pregnancy is uncertain. Then, on the fifth day, [he offers] a mess of cooked grain for Nirṛti in the house of the discarded wife, [prepared] from black rice torn by the fingernails.

12.5.92.s: kṛṣṇāṃ kūṭāṃ dadāti | atha ṣaṣṭhe 'hny āgneyam aṣṭākapālam̐ senānyo gṛhe
12.5.92.d: कृष्णां कूटां ददाति । अथ षष्ठे ऽह्न्य् आग्नेयम् अष्टाकपालँ सेनान्यो गृहे
12.5.92.m: He gives a black, hornless cow. Then, on the sixth day, [he offers a cake] on eight potsherds for Agni in the house of the commander of the army.

12.5.92.s: hiraṇyaṃ dadāti | atha saptame 'hni vāruṇaṃ daśakapālam̐ sūtasya gṛhe
12.5.92.d: हिरण्यं ददाति । अथ सप्तमे ऽह्नि वारुणं दशकपालँ सूतस्य गृहे
12.5.92.m: He gives gold. Then, on the seventh day, [he offers a cake] on ten potsherds for Varuṇa in the house of the charioteer.

12.5.92.s: mahāniraṣṭaṃ dadāti | athāṣṭame 'hni mārutam̐ saptakapālaṃ grāmaṇyo gṛhe
12.5.92.d: महानिरष्टं ददाति । अथाष्टमे ऽह्नि मारुतँ सप्तकपालं ग्रामण्यो गृहे
12.5.92.m: He gives a castrated bull. Then, on the eighth day, [he offers a cake] on seven potsherds for the Maruts in the house of the village headman.

12.5.92.s: pṛśniṃ dadāti | atha navame 'hni sāvitraṃ dvādaśakapālaṃ kṣattur gṛhe |
12.5.92.d: पृश्निं ददाति । अथ नवमे ऽह्नि सावित्रं द्वादशकपालं क्षत्तुर् गृहे ।
12.5.92.m: He gives a spotted [cow]. Then, on the ninth day, [he offers a cake] on twelve potsherds for Savitar in the house of the chamberlain.

12.5.92.s: upadhvastaṃ dadāti | atha daśame 'hny āśvinaṃ dvikapālam̐ saṃgrahītur gṛhe
12.5.92.d: उपध्वस्तं ददाति । अथ दशमे ऽह्न्य् आश्विनं द्विकपालँ संग्रहीतुर् गृहे
12.5.92.m: He gives a dusty-coloured [bull]. Then, on the tenth day, [he offers a cake] on two potsherds for the Aśvins in the house of the collector.

12.5.92.s: savātyau dadāti | athaikādaśe 'hni pauṣṇaṃ caruṃ bhāgadughasya gṛhe
12.5.92.d: सवात्यौ ददाति । अथैकादशे ऽह्नि पौष्णं चरुं भागदुघस्य गृहे
12.5.92.m: He gives two born of the same womb. Then, on the eleventh day, [he offers] a mess of cooked grain for Pūṣan in the house of the distributor of shares.

12.5.92.s: śyāmaṃ dadāti | atha dvādaśe 'hni raudraṃ gāvīdhukaṃ carum akṣāvāpasya gṛhe
12.5.92.d: श्यामं ददाति । अथ द्वादशे ऽह्नि रौद्रं गावीधुकं चरुम् अक्षावापस्य गृहे
12.5.92.m: He gives a dark-grey [bull]. Then, on the twelfth day, [he offers] a mess of cooked gavidhukā grain for Rudra in the house of the superintendent of dicing.

12.5.92.s: śabalamudvāraṃ dadāti prasiddham evāsyaitad ahaḥ śvetāyai śvetavatsāyai payo dohayitvā samātacyaiva nidadhāti |
12.5.92.d: शबलमुद्वारं ददाति प्रसिद्धम् एवास्यैतद् अहः श्वेतायै श्वेतवत्सायै पयो दोहयित्वा समातच्यैव निदधाति ।
12.5.92.m: He gives a dappled one whose tail is white at the end. In the known manner, on this day, having milked the milk of a white cow with a white calf, [and] having curdled it, he sets it aside.
Then, on the thirteenth day, the ritual for Mitra and Bṛhaspati takes place.

12.6.92.s: atha vai bhavati śvetāyai śvetavatsāyai dugdhe svayaṃmūrte svayaṃmathita ājya āśvatthe pātre catuḥsraktau svayamavapannāyai śākhāyai karṇām̐ś cākarṇām̐ś ca taṇḍulān vicinuyāt | iti |
12.6.92.d: अथ वै भवति श्वेतायै श्वेतवत्सायै दुग्धे स्वयंमूर्ते स्वयंमथित आज्य आश्वत्थे पात्रे चतुःस्रक्तौ स्वयमवपन्नायै शाखायै कर्णाँश् चाकर्णाँश् च तण्डुलान् विचिनुयात् । इति ।
12.6.92.m: Now indeed there is [the brāhmaṇa passage]: 'In milk from a white cow with a white calf, in self-coagulated, self-churned ghee, in a four-cornered aśvattha vessel, from a branch fallen of itself, he should separate the broken and unbroken grains of rice.'

12.6.92.s: atha vai bhavati svayaṃkṛtā vedir bhavati svayaṃdinaṃ barhiḥ svayaṃkṛta idhmas | iti
12.6.92.d: अथ वै भवति स्वयंकृता वेदिर् भवति स्वयंदिनं बर्हिः स्वयंकृत इध्मस् । इति
12.6.92.m: Now indeed there is [the brāhmaṇa passage]: 'The altar is self-made, the sacrificial grass is cut by itself, the kindling wood is self-made.'
This king himself is honoured through [these] acts.

12.6.92.s: sa svayam eva vediṃ karoti svayam idhmābarhiḥ saṃnahyati svayam āśvatthaṃ pātraṃ catuḥsraktiṃ karoti svayam avapannāyai śākhāyai karṇām̐ś cākarṇām̐ś ca taṇḍulān vicinoti |
12.6.92.d: स स्वयम् एव वेदिं करोति स्वयम् इध्माबर्हिः संनह्यति स्वयम् आश्वत्थं पात्रं चतुःस्रक्तिं करोति स्वयम् अवपन्नायै शाखायै कर्णाँश् चाकर्णाँश् च तण्डुलान् विचिनोति ।
12.6.92.m: He himself makes the altar; he himself ties the kindling wood and the sacrificial grass; he himself makes the four-cornered aśvattha vessel; he himself separates the broken and unbroken rice grains from the branch that fell by itself.

12.6.93.s: atha vai bhavati ye karṇāḥ sa payasi bārhaspatyo ye 'karṇāḥ sa ājye maitras | iti |
12.6.93.d: अथ वै भवति ये कर्णाः स पयसि बार्हस्पत्यो ये ऽकर्णाः स आज्ये मैत्रस् । इति ।
12.6.93.m: Now indeed there is [the brāhmaṇa passage]: 'Those which are broken grains, that [mess] is for Bṛhaspati in milk; those which are unbroken, that [mess] is for Mitra in ghee.'

12.6.93.s: athottarato bhasmamiśrān aṅgārān nirūhya teṣu navaṃ pātram adhiśritya tiraḥ pavitram ājyam ānīya tiraḥ pavitram akarṇānopya tena bārhaspatyam apidadhāti
12.6.93.d: अथोत्तरतो भस्ममिश्रान् अङ्गारान् निरूह्य तेषु नवं पात्रम् अधिश्रित्य तिरः पवित्रम् आज्यम् आनीय तिरः पवित्रम् अकर्णानोप्य तेन बार्हस्पत्यम् अपिदधाति
12.6.93.m: Then, having scraped out embers mixed with ashes to the north, having placed a new vessel on them, having poured in ghee through the purifier, [and] having scattered the unbroken grains through the purifier, he covers the [mess] for Bṛhaspati with it.
He places it, thus covered, inside the altar.

12.6.93.s: samānaṃ karmā prayājebhyaḥ pañca prayājān iṣṭvodaṅṅ atyākramya sam̐srāveṇa bārhaspatyam abhighārya maitram abhighārayati
12.6.93.d: समानं कर्मा प्रयाजेभ्यः पञ्च प्रयाजान् इष्ट्वोदङ्ङ् अत्याक्रम्य सँस्रावेण बार्हस्पत्यम् अभिघार्य मैत्रम् अभिघारयति
12.6.93.m: The ritual is the same up to the fore-offerings. Having offered the five fore-offerings, having stepped across to the north, having basted the [mess] for Bṛhaspati with the residue, he bastes the [mess] for Mitra.

12.6.93.s: bārhaspatyena pūrveṇa pracaraty atha maitreṇa bārhaspatyasya pūrvasya sviṣṭakṛte 'vadyaty atha maitrasya
12.6.93.d: बार्हस्पत्येन पूर्वेण प्रचरत्य् अथ मैत्रेण बार्हस्पत्यस्य पूर्वस्य स्विष्टकृते ऽवद्यत्य् अथ मैत्रस्य
12.6.93.m: He performs the ritual first with the [mess] for Bṛhaspati, then with that for Mitra. He cuts portions for the Sviṣṭakṛt first from the [mess] for Bṛhaspati, then from that for Mitra.
He cuts portions of the iḍā first from the [mess] for Bṛhaspati, then from that for Mitra.

12.6.93.s: anvāhāryam āsādyaitām eva śvetām̐ śvetavatsāṃ dadāti
12.6.93.d: अन्वाहार्यम् आसाद्यैताम् एव श्वेताँ श्वेतवत्सां ददाति
12.6.93.m: Having placed the anvāhārya cooked rice, he gives that very white cow with a white calf.
The oblation for Mitra and Bṛhaspati is concluded.

12.7.93.m: Then, in this very first half of the month, he undergoes consecration for the Abhiṣecanīya in the form of an ukthya sacrifice.

12.7.93.s: tasyāparimitā dīkṣāḥ ṣaḍ upasadaḥ sa tathā rājānaṃ krīṇāti yathā manyate 'māvāsyāyai me yajñiye 'han sutyā saṃpatsyata iti
12.7.93.d: तस्यापरिमिता दीक्षाः षड् उपसदः स तथा राजानं क्रीणाति यथा मन्यते ऽमावास्यायै मे यज्ञिये ऽहन् सुत्या संपत्स्यत इति
12.7.93.m: For it there are unmeasured consecrations [and] six upasad days. He buys King [Soma] in such a way as he thinks: 'My soma pressing will fall on the new-moon day, on a day fit for sacrifice.'

12.7.94.s: tasya tayā saṃpadyate | atha prāyaṇīyena carati prāyaṇīyena caritvā padena carati
12.7.94.d: तस्य तया संपद्यते । अथ प्रायणीयेन चरति प्रायणीयेन चरित्वा पदेन चरति
12.7.94.m: For him it falls on that [day]. Then he performs the opening offering. Having performed the opening offering, he performs the ritual with the [cow's] footprint.

12.7.94.s: padena caritvā rohite carmaṇi rājānaṃ krītvohyātithyaṃ nirvapati |
12.7.94.d: पदेन चरित्वा रोहिते चर्मणि राजानं क्रीत्वोह्यातिथ्यं निर्वपति ।
12.7.94.m: Having performed the ritual with the footprint, having bought King [Soma] on a red hide, [and] having brought him near, he prepares an offering for the guest oblation.
Having performed the ritual with the guest oblation, he then proceeds day by day with the upasad offerings.

12.7.94.s: athāhavanīyaṃ praṇayati | āhavanīyaṃ praṇīya rathavāhane sadohavirdhāne saṃminoti
12.7.94.d: अथाहवनीयं प्रणयति । आहवनीयं प्रणीय रथवाहने सदोहविर्धाने संमिनोति
12.7.94.m:
Then he brings forward the āhavanīya fire. Having brought forward the āhavanīya fire, he erects the two chariot-stands, the sadas shed, and the havirdhāna shed.

Having erected the two chariot-stands, the sadas shed, and the havirdhāna shed, he conducts Agni and Soma forward.
Having conducted Agni and Soma forward, he raises the sacrificial post according to the procedure of the sacrificial post.

12.7.94.s: svarvantaṃ yūpam utsṛjyāgnīṣomīyaṃ paśum upākaroti tasya prasiddhaṃ vapayā caritvā vasatīvarīr gṛhṇāti |
12.7.94.d: स्वर्वन्तं यूपम् उत्सृज्याग्नीषोमीयं पशुम् उपाकरोति तस्य प्रसिद्धं वपया चरित्वा वसतीवरीर् गृह्णाति ।
12.7.94.m: Having set up the sacrificial post equipped with its top-ring, he dedicates the victim for Agni and Soma. Having performed the ritual with its omentum in the established manner, he takes up the vasatīvarī waters.
Then he prepares an offering of the animal cake.

12.7.94.s: tam anuvartante 'ṣṭau devasuvām̐ havīm̐ṣi | agnaye gṛhapataye | ity etāni
12.7.94.d: तम् अनुवर्तन्ते ऽष्टौ देवसुवाँ हवीँषि । अग्नये गृहपतये । इत्य् एतानि
12.7.94.m: The eight oblations of the divine vivifiers accompany it, namely those [beginning with]: 'To Agni, lord of the house.'

12.7.94.s: teṣām uktaṃ caraṇaṃ yathāgner vidhāyām iḍāntāḥ puroḍāśāḥ saṃtiṣṭhante
12.7.94.d: तेषाम् उक्तं चरणं यथाग्नेर् विधायाम् इडान्ताः पुरोडाशाः संतिष्ठन्ते
12.7.94.m: The procedure for them has been explained as in the ritual arrangement of the fire altar. The cakes conclude with the iḍā.

12.7.94.s: patnīsaṃyājāntaḥ paśus | hṛdayaśūlānta ity eke | atraitān dundubhīn anudiśam āsañjayati |
12.7.94.d: पत्नीसंयाजान्तः पशुस् । हृदयशूलान्त इत्य् एके । अत्रैतान् दुन्दुभीन् अनुदिशम् आसञ्जयति ।
12.7.94.m: The animal sacrifice concludes with the offerings to the wives of the gods; according to some, it concludes with the heart-spit. Here he hangs up these drums in every direction.
Then, having carried the vasatīvarī waters around, having set aside the milk, they observe the fast.

12.7.94.s: athāto mahārātra eva budhyanta prātarājyāni gṛhītvā rājānam upāvahṛtya prātaranuvākam upākaroti
12.7.94.d: अथातो महारात्र एव बुध्यन्त प्रातराज्यानि गृहीत्वा राजानम् उपावहृत्य प्रातरनुवाकम् उपाकरोति
12.7.94.m: Then, waking up at the deep of the night itself, taking the morning clarified butter, bringing down the king [soma], he commences the morning recitation.
When the morning recitation has been enclosed, he goes toward the waters.
He comes up with the waters; he undertakes the ukthya rite.

12.7.94.s: prasiddho 'bhiṣavaḥ prasiddhaṃ grahā gṛhyante samānaṃ karmāśvinād grahāt |
12.7.94.d: प्रसिद्धो ऽभिषवः प्रसिद्धं ग्रहा गृह्यन्ते समानं कर्माश्विनाद् ग्रहात् ।
12.7.94.m: The pressing is familiar; the soma-cups are drawn as usual; the ritual is the same up to the soma-cup for the Aśvins.

12.7.94.s: āśvinaṃ grahaṃ gṛhītvā dve raśane ādāya yūpam abhyaiti
12.7.94.d: आश्विनं ग्रहं गृहीत्वा द्वे रशने आदाय यूपम् अभ्यैति
12.7.94.m: Having drawn the soma-cup for the Aśvins, taking two cords, he approaches the sacrificial post.

12.7.94.s: svarvantaṃ yūpam utsṛjyāgneyaṃ paśum upākaroti tasyaidnrāgna upālambhyo bhavati
12.7.94.d: स्वर्वन्तं यूपम् उत्सृज्याग्नेयं पशुम् उपाकरोति तस्यैद्न्राग्न उपालम्भ्यो भवति
12.7.94.m: Having touched the sun-lit sacrificial post, he dedicates the animal victim to Agni; an additional victim to Indra-Agni is to be sacrificed for it.

12.7.94.s: tayoḥ prasiddhaṃ vapābhyāṃ caritvā prasarpanti prātaḥsavanāya
12.7.94.d: तयोः प्रसिद्धं वपाभ्यां चरित्वा प्रसर्पन्ति प्रातःसवनाय
12.7.94.m: Having performed the rites of their two omenta as usual, they glide forward for the morning pressing.

12.7.95.s: tad ṛjudhā saṃtiṣṭhate prasarpanti mādhyaṃdināya savanāya
12.7.95.d: तद् ऋजुधा संतिष्ठते प्रसर्पन्ति माध्यंदिनाय सवनाय
12.7.95.m: That concludes straightforwardly. They glide forward for the midday pressing.

12.7.95.s: prasiddho 'bhiṣavaḥ prasiddhaṃ grahā gṛhyante samānaṃ karmā dākṣiṇebhyas |
12.7.95.d: प्रसिद्धो ऽभिषवः प्रसिद्धं ग्रहा गृह्यन्ते समानं कर्मा दाक्षिणेभ्यस् ।
12.7.95.m: The pressing is familiar; the soma-cups are drawn as usual; the ritual is the same up to the offerings of priestly gifts.

12.7.95.s: dākṣiṇāni hoṣyan yācaty ājyasthālīm̐ sasruvām̐ srucaṃ vāsas
12.7.95.d: दाक्षिणानि होष्यन् याचत्य् आज्यस्थालीँ सस्रुवाँ स्रुचं वासस्
12.7.95.m: Intending to offer the priestly gifts, he asks for the clarified butter pot with the dipping spoon, the offering ladle, and a cloth.

12.7.95.s: tasyaitasya vasanasyāntamāyāṃ daśāyāṃ niṣkarajjuḥ pragrathitā bhavati |
12.7.95.d: तस्यैतस्य वसनस्यान्तमायां दशायां निष्करज्जुः प्रग्रथिता भवति ।
12.7.95.m: To the edge fringe of this cloth, a string of coins is tied.

12.7.95.s: etat samādāyāha | ehi yajamāna | iti | uttareṇāgnīdhrīyaṃ parītyottareṇa sadaḥ parītyāgreṇa śālāṃ tiṣṭhate pratiprasthātra etāni śastrāṇi prayacchati |
12.7.95.d: एतत् समादायाह । एहि यजमान । इति । उत्तरेणाग्नीध्रीयं परीत्योत्तरेण सदः परीत्याग्रेण शालां तिष्ठते प्रतिप्रस्थात्र एतानि शस्त्राणि प्रयच्छति ।
12.7.95.m: Taking this up, he says: 'Come, sacrificer!' Having walked around the north of the āgnīdhrīya fire, having walked around the north of the sadas shed, he stands in front of the hall and hands over these weapons to the pratiprasthātṛ priest.

12.7.95.s: athāha | ehi yajamāna | iti ratha eṣa dakṣiṇe śroṇyante rathavāhana āhito bhavati
12.7.95.d: अथाह । एहि यजमान । इति रथ एष दक्षिणे श्रोण्यन्ते रथवाहन आहितो भवति
12.7.95.m: Then he says: 'Come, sacrificer!' This chariot is mounted on a chariot-carrier at the southern corner of the hip.

12.7.95.s: tam upāvaharati | indrasya vajro 'si vārtraghnas tvayāyaṃ vṛtraṃ vadhyāt | iti |
12.7.95.d: तम् उपावहरति । इन्द्रस्य वज्रो ऽसि वार्त्रघ्नस् त्वयायं वृत्रं वध्यात् । इति ।
12.7.95.m: He takes it down with: 'You are Indra's thunderbolt, slayer of Vṛtra; with you may this [sacrificer] slay Vṛtra.'
Then, seized by the yoke, they roll it down silently inside the altar.
Then he washes the horses with water silently.

12.7.95.s: atha dakṣiṇaṃ yogyaṃ yunakti mitrāvaruṇayos tvā praśāstroḥ praśiṣā yunajmi yajñasya yogena | iti |
12.7.95.d: अथ दक्षिणं योग्यं युनक्ति मित्रावरुणयोस् त्वा प्रशास्त्रोः प्रशिषा युनज्मि यज्ञस्य योगेन । इति ।
12.7.95.m: Then he yokes the right horse with: 'By the command of Mitra and Varuṇa, the two directors, I yoke you with the yoking of the sacrifice.'
Then he strokes its back silently.

12.7.95.s: evam evottaraṃ yogyaṃ yunakti tasyaivam evottarataḥ praṣṭim upaniyunakti
12.7.95.d: एवम् एवोत्तरं योग्यं युनक्ति तस्यैवम् एवोत्तरतः प्रष्टिम् उपनियुनक्ति
12.7.95.m: Just so he yokes the left horse. Just so he yokes the side horse to its left.

12.7.95.s: tayor evam eva pṛṣṭhe marmṛjyate | etasya yogam anu sarvam āṇivad yujyate |
12.7.95.d: तयोर् एवम् एव पृष्ठे मर्मृज्यते । एतस्य योगम् अनु सर्वम् आणिवद् युज्यते ।
12.7.95.m: Just so he strokes the backs of both of them. Following its yoking, everything is joined to the axle-pin.
They place girths on the elephants; they pack bundles of garments.

12.7.95.s: vasanānāṃ daśāsu niṣkarajjūḥ pragrathnanti pūgaśo dakṣiṇā āyātayati |
12.7.95.d: वसनानां दशासु निष्करज्जूः प्रग्रथ्नन्ति पूगशो दक्षिणा आयातयति ।
12.7.95.m: They tie strings of coins to the fringes of the garments; he brings the priestly gifts up in groups.
Then he offers into the gārhapatya fire with two verses to Sūrya.

12.7.96.m: He offers into the āgnīdhra fire with a verse containing the word 'naya'. The priestly gifts are released along the path of the priestly gifts.

12.7.96.s: sa yat kiṃcid dadāti hiraṇyamukham eva dadāti | atha vāsām̐sy atha yuktāni goaśvam̐ hastipuruṣam antatas |
12.7.96.d: स यत् किंचिद् ददाति हिरण्यमुखम् एव ददाति । अथ वासाँस्य् अथ युक्तानि गोअश्वँ हस्तिपुरुषम् अन्ततस् ।
12.7.96.m: Whatever he gives, he gives only with gold in front; then garments, then yoked [animals], cattle and horses, and at last elephants and men.
These chariots, remaining un-given, are for running beyond.

12.7.96.s: naite 'nyasya santa ājiṃ dhāvanti manasaiva svaratham adhvaryave dadāti
12.7.96.d: नैते ऽन्यस्य सन्त आजिं धावन्ति मनसैव स्वरथम् अध्वर्यवे ददाति
12.7.96.m: These do not run the race belonging to someone else. He mentally gives his own chariot to the adhvaryu priest.
Mentally he assigns a four-footed field to the brahman priest.

12.7.96.s: manasā samanudiśya dakṣiṇās tribhir marutvatīyaiś carati
12.7.96.d: मनसा समनुदिश्य दक्षिणास् त्रिभिर् मरुत्वतीयैश् चरति
12.7.96.m: Having mentally assigned the priestly gifts, he proceeds with the three cups for Indra Marutvat.

12.7.96.s: sīdanti nārāśam̐sā āpyāyitā dakṣiṇasya havirdhānasyāpālambam adho'dho mahendrāya ||
12.7.96.d: सीदन्ति नाराशँसा आप्यायिता दक्षिणस्य हविर्धानस्यापालम्बम् अधोऽधो महेन्द्राय ॥
12.7.96.m: The replenished nārāśaṃsa cups are set down beneath the axle-prop of the southern havirdhāna shed, downwards for Mahendra.

12.8.96.s: atha yācati vaitasaṃ droṇakalaśam̐ ṣoḍaśa vāyavyāni |
12.8.96.d: अथ याचति वैतसं द्रोणकलशँ षोडश वायव्यानि ।
12.8.96.m: Then he asks for a cane trough-vessel and sixteen wooden cups.

12.8.96.s: athāsyaitat purastād eva ṣoḍaśatayya āpo digbhyaḥ saṃbhṛtā dakṣiṇasya havirdhānasya prācyo 'kṣāt pratīcya upastambhanān nihitāḥ śerate
12.8.96.d: अथास्यैतत् पुरस्ताद् एव षोडशतय्य आपो दिग्भ्यः संभृता दक्षिणस्य हविर्धानस्य प्राच्यो ऽक्षात् प्रतीच्य उपस्तम्भनान् निहिताः शेरते
12.8.96.m: Now beforehand, these sixteen kinds of water, collected from the quarters, have been placed and lie between the east of the axle and the west of the axle-prop of the southern havirdhāna shed.

12.8.97.d: तासां वहन्त्यः पूर्वार्ध्या भवन्ति सारस्वत्यो ऽपरार्ध्याः
12.8.97.m: Of them, the flowing ones are on the eastern side, and those from the Sarasvatī are on the western side.

12.8.97.s: sa vahantīr abhijuhoti | artheta stha | apo devīr madhumatīr agṛhṇan | ūrjasvatī rājasūyāya citānāḥ | yābhir mitrāvaruṇāv abhyaṣiñcan yābhir indram anayann aty arātīḥ || rāṣṭradā stha rāṣṭraṃ datta svāha | iti
12.8.97.d: स वहन्तीर् अभिजुहोति । अर्थेत स्थ । अपो देवीर् मधुमतीर् अगृह्णन् । ऊर्जस्वती राजसूयाय चितानाः । याभिर् मित्रावरुणाव् अभ्यषिञ्चन् याभिर् इन्द्रम् अनयन्न् अत्य् अरातीः ॥ राष्ट्रदा स्थ राष्ट्रं दत्त स्वाह । इति
12.8.97.m: He makes an offering over the flowing waters with: 'You are with a purpose; the divine waters, honeyed, have been seized, vigorous, gathered for the royal consecration; with which they consecrated Mitra and Varuṇa, with which they carried Indra past enemies; you are bestowers of dominion, bestow dominion, svāhā!'

12.8.97.s: gṛhṇāti parṇamayena rāṣṭradā stha rāṣṭram amuṣmā āmuṣyāyaṇāyāmuṣya putrāyāmuṣya pautrāya datta | iti |
12.8.97.d: गृह्णाति पर्णमयेन राष्ट्रदा स्थ राष्ट्रम् अमुष्मा आमुष्यायणायामुष्य पुत्रायामुष्य पौत्राय दत्त । इति ।
12.8.97.m: He takes [them] with a palāśa ladle with: 'You are bestowers of dominion; bestow dominion upon NN, of such-and-such lineage, son of NN, grandson of NN!'

12.8.97.s: apāṃ patir asi | ity apāṃpatīyāḥ puṃnāmno votsasya samudriyā vā
12.8.97.d: अपां पतिर् असि । इत्य् अपांपतीयाः पुंनाम्नो वोत्सस्य समुद्रिया वा
12.8.97.m: With: 'You are the lord of waters', [he draws] the waters of the lord of waters, or from a spring of masculine name, or sea waters.
With: 'You are a bull wave', [he draws] waters of a wave.

12.8.97.s: vṛṣaseno 'si | iti palvalyās | vrajakṣita stha | iti kūpyās | marutām oja stha | iti niveṣṭyāḥ
12.8.97.d: वृषसेनो ऽसि । इति पल्वल्यास् । व्रजक्षित स्थ । इति कूप्यास् । मरुताम् ओज स्थ । इति निवेष्ट्याः
12.8.97.m: With: 'You are a bull-army', [he draws] pool waters. With: 'You are dweller in the pen', [he draws] well waters. With: 'You are the might of the Maruts', [he draws] whirlpool waters.

12.8.97.s: sūryavarcasa stha | ity atidṛśyāḥ sūryatvacasa stha | ity ātapati varṣyās |
12.8.97.d: सूर्यवर्चस स्थ । इत्य् अतिदृश्याः सूर्यत्वचस स्थ । इत्य् आतपति वर्ष्यास् ।
12.8.97.m: With: 'You are radiant as the sun', [he draws] clear-flowing waters. With: 'You are sun-skinned', [he draws] rainwaters falling while the sun shines.

12.8.97.s: māndā stha | iti hrādunyas | vāśā stha | iti pṛsvāḥ
12.8.97.d: मान्दा स्थ । इति ह्रादुन्यस् । वाशा स्थ । इति पृस्वाः
12.8.97.m: With: 'You are refreshing', [he draws] hail waters. With: 'You are roaring', [he draws] frost waters.

12.8.97.s: śakvarī stha | iti gorulbyās | viśvabhṛta stha | iti payas | janabhṛta stha | iti dadhi |
12.8.97.d: शक्वरी स्थ । इति गोरुल्ब्यास् । विश्वभृत स्थ । इति पयस् । जनभृत स्थ । इति दधि ।
12.8.97.m: With: 'You are the powerful ones', [he draws] fluid from the cow's afterbirth. With: 'You are all-supporting', [he draws] milk. With: 'You are people-supporting', [he draws] curds.

12.8.97.s: agnes tejasyā stha | ity ājyam apām oṣadhīnām̐ rasa stha | iti madhu | atha sārasvatīr abhijuhoti | apo devīr madhumatīr agṛhṇan | ūrjasvatī rājasūyāya citānāḥ | yābhir mitrāvaruṇāv abhyaṣiñcan yābhir indram anayann aty arātīḥ || rāṣṭradā stha rāṣṭraṃ datta svāhā | iti
12.8.97.d: अग्नेस् तेजस्या स्थ । इत्य् आज्यम् अपाम् ओषधीनाँ रस स्थ । इति मधु । अथ सारस्वतीर् अभिजुहोति । अपो देवीर् मधुमतीर् अगृह्णन् । ऊर्जस्वती राजसूयाय चितानाः । याभिर् मित्रावरुणाव् अभ्यषिञ्चन् याभिर् इन्द्रम् अनयन्न् अत्य् अरातीः ॥ राष्ट्रदा स्थ राष्ट्रं दत्त स्वाहा । इति
12.8.97.m: With: 'You are fiery energy of Agni', [he draws] clarified butter. With: 'You are the sap of waters and plants', [he draws] honey. Then he offers over the Sarasvatī waters with: 'The divine waters, honeyed, have been seized, vigorous, gathered for the royal consecration; with which they consecrated Mitra and Varuṇa, with which they carried Indra past enemies; you are bestowers of dominion, bestow dominion, svāhā!'

12.8.98.s: gṛhṇāti parṇamayena rāṣṭradā stha rāṣṭram amuṣmā āmuṣyāyaṇāyāmuṣya putrāyāmuṣya pautrāya datta | iti |
12.8.98.d: गृह्णाति पर्णमयेन राष्ट्रदा स्थ राष्ट्रम् अमुष्मा आमुष्यायणायामुष्य पुत्रायामुष्य पौत्राय दत्त । इति ।
12.8.98.m: He takes [them] with a palāśa ladle with: 'You are bestowers of dominion; bestow dominion upon NN, of such-and-such lineage, son of NN, grandson of NN!'

12.8.98.s: athainā vaitase droṇakalaśe samavanayati devīr āpaḥ saṃ madhumatīr madhumatībhiḥ sṛjyadhvam | mahi varcaḥ kṣatriyāya vanvānās | iti |
12.8.98.d: अथैना वैतसे द्रोणकलशे समवनयति देवीर् आपः सं मधुमतीर् मधुमतीभिः सृज्यध्वम् । महि वर्चः क्षत्रियाय वन्वानास् । इति ।
12.8.98.m: Then he pours them together into the cane trough-vessel with: 'Divine waters, honeyed, mingle with the honeyed ones, winning great splendor for the kṣatriya!'

12.8.98.s: athainā antareṇa hotuś ca dhiṣṇiyaṃ brāhmaṇāccham̐sinaś ca sādayati | anādhṛṣṭāḥ sīdatorjasvatīr mahi varcaḥ kṣatriyāya dadhatīs | iti |
12.8.98.d: अथैना अन्तरेण होतुश् च धिष्णियं ब्राह्मणाच्छँसिनश् च सादयति । अनाधृष्टाः सीदतोर्जस्वतीर् महि वर्चः क्षत्रियाय दधतीस् । इति ।
12.8.98.m: Then he sets them down between the hearth of the hotṛ priest and the brāhmaṇācchaṃsin priest with: 'Unassailed, dwell, vigorous, granting great splendor to the kṣatriya!'

12.8.98.s: atra ye 'rthyāḥ prarekā adhvaryos tān āvasatham̐ haranti | atha ye 'narthyā apas tān abhyavaharanti
12.8.98.d: अत्र ये ऽर्थ्याः प्ररेका अध्वर्योस् तान् आवसथँ हरन्ति । अथ ये ऽनर्थ्या अपस् तान् अभ्यवहरन्ति
12.8.98.m: Then, those waters which are useful remainders for the adhvaryu priest, they carry to his dwelling; then those which are not useful, they throw away into the water.
Of the Sarasvatī waters upon which no offering was made, they reserve the vasatīvarī waters for the Daśapeya sacrifice.

12.9.98.s: athātraiva tiṣṭhan yācati darbhanāḍīm̐ śatamānam̐ hiraṇyaṃ catvāri nānāvṛkṣyāṇi pātrāṇi tārpyaṃ coṣṇīṣaṃ caikaśataṃ ca darbhapuñjīlāni dadhy udumbaram̐ śaṣpāṇi dhanuś ceṣūm̐ś ceti
12.9.98.d: अथात्रैव तिष्ठन् याचति दर्भनाडीँ शतमानँ हिरण्यं चत्वारि नानावृक्ष्याणि पात्राणि तार्प्यं चोष्णीषं चैकशतं च दर्भपुञ्जीलानि दध्य् उदुम्बरँ शष्पाणि धनुश् चेषूँश् चेति
12.9.98.m: Then, standing right there, he asks for a darbha reed, a gold piece weighing a hundred mānas, four vessels made of different woods, a tārpya garment, a turban, one hundred and one darbha tufts, curds, udumbara wood, sprouts of barley, and a bow and arrows.

12.9.98.s: sa darbhanāḍyām̐ śatamānam̐ hiraṇyaṃ pragrathnāti | anibhṛṣṭam asi vāco bandhus tapojās | iti |
12.9.98.d: स दर्भनाड्याँ शतमानँ हिरण्यं प्रग्रथ्नाति । अनिभृष्टम् असि वाचो बन्धुस् तपोजास् । इति ।
12.9.98.m: He ties the gold piece of a hundred mānas inside the darbha reed with: 'You are unassailed, the friend of speech, born of heat.'

12.9.98.s: athainad vaitase droṇakalaśe 'vadadhāti somasya dātram asi | iti
12.9.98.d: अथैनद् वैतसे द्रोणकलशे ऽवदधाति सोमस्य दात्रम् असि । इति
12.9.98.m: Then he places it in the cane trough-vessel with: 'You are the gift of Soma.'

12.9.99.s: hiraṇyenotpunāti śukrā vaḥ śukreṇot punāmi candrāś candreṇa | amṛtā amṛtena svāhā rājasūyāya citānās | iti
12.9.99.d: हिरण्येनोत्पुनाति शुक्रा वः शुक्रेणोत् पुनामि चन्द्राश् चन्द्रेण । अमृता अमृतेन स्वाहा राजसूयाय चितानास् । इति
12.9.99.m: He strains [the waters] with gold with: 'Bright, I purify you with the bright; shining, with the shining; immortal, with the immortal; svāhā, gathered for the royal consecration!'

12.9.99.s: gṛhṇāti parṇamayena sadhamādo dyumninīr ūrja etā anibhṛṣṭā apasyuvo vasānaḥ | pastyāsu cakre varuṇaḥ sadhastham apām̐ śiśur mātṛtamāsv antar iti
12.9.99.d: गृह्णाति पर्णमयेन सधमादो द्युम्निनीर् ऊर्ज एता अनिभृष्टा अपस्युवो वसानः । पस्त्यासु चक्रे वरुणः सधस्थम् अपाँ शिशुर् मातृतमास्व् अन्तर् इति
12.9.99.m: He draws [them] with the palāśa ladle with: 'These are the fellow-revelers, the glorious, the vigorous waters, which uninjured, working, he puts on; Varuṇa has made his dwelling in the settlements, the child of waters within the most motherly ones.'

12.9.99.s: purastād āsīnāya brahmaṇe prayacchaty etayaiva gṛhītvā dakṣiṇata āsīnāyaudumbareṇa rājanyāya prayacchati |
12.9.99.d: पुरस्ताद् आसीनाय ब्रह्मणे प्रयच्छत्य् एतयैव गृहीत्वा दक्षिणत आसीनायौदुम्बरेण राजन्याय प्रयच्छति ।
12.9.99.m: He hands [a cup] to the brahman priest seated in front; taking [the liquid] with that very same [vessel], he hands it with an udumbara [cup] to the nobleman seated to the south.

12.9.99.s: etayaiva gṛhītvā paścād āsīnāyāśvatthena vaiśyāya prayacchati |
12.9.99.d: एतयैव गृहीत्वा पश्चाद् आसीनायाश्वत्थेन वैश्याय प्रयच्छति ।
12.9.99.m: Taking [it] with that very same [vessel], he hands it with an aśvattha [cup] to the vaiśya seated to the west.

12.9.99.s: etayaiva gṛhītvottarata āsīnāya naiyagrodhena janyāya prayacchati |
12.9.99.d: एतयैव गृहीत्वोत्तरत आसीनाय नैयग्रोधेन जन्याय प्रयच्छति ।
12.9.99.m: Taking [it] with that very same [vessel], he hands it with a nyagrodha [cup] to the man of the people seated to the north.

12.9.99.s: athaitaṃ prarekam āgnīdhram̐ hṛtvāpidhāya prajñātaṃ nidadhāti |
12.9.99.d: अथैतं प्ररेकम् आग्नीध्रँ हृत्वापिधाय प्रज्ञातं निदधाति ।
12.9.99.m: Then, having carried this residue to the āgnīdhra [shed] and covered it, he places it in a known place.

12.9.99.s: atha yajamānaṃ tārpyaṃ paridhāpayati kṣatrasyolbam asi | iti
12.9.99.d: अथ यजमानं तार्प्यं परिधापयति क्षत्रस्योल्बम् असि । इति
12.9.99.m: Then he clothes the sacrificer in a tārpya garment with: 'You are the outer covering of dominion.'

12.9.99.s: kṣatrasya yonir asi | ity āsajate tārpyam
12.9.99.d: क्षत्रस्य योनिर् असि । इत्य् आसजते तार्प्यम्
12.9.99.m: With 'You are the womb of dominion,' he fastens the tārpya garment.

12.9.99.s: abhīva nābhim uṣṇīṣaṃ paryasyati | athainam ekaśatena darbhapuñjīlaiḥ pavayati nityena pavanena |
12.9.99.d: अभीव नाभिम् उष्णीषं पर्यस्यति । अथैनम् एकशतेन दर्भपुञ्जीलैः पवयति नित्येन पवनेन ।
12.9.99.m: He wraps the turban around about the navel. Then he purifies him with one hundred and one stalks of darbha grass, with the regular purification.

12.9.99.s: athainam unmṛjann āśayati dadhy udumbaram̐ śaṣpāṇīti |
12.9.99.d: अथैनम् उन्मृजन्न् आशयति दध्य् उदुम्बरँ शष्पाणीति ।
12.9.99.m: Then, wiping him down, he makes him consume curds, udumbara, and sprouted grasses.

12.9.99.s: athainam āvidbhiḥ prāñcam ānayati | āvinno agnir gṛhapatis iti saptabhir anucchandasam
12.9.99.d: अथैनम् आविद्भिः प्राञ्चम् आनयति । आविन्नो अग्निर् गृहपतिस् इति सप्तभिर् अनुच्छन्दसम्
12.9.99.m: Then he leads him eastward with the proclamations, with the seven [formulas] according to their meters: 'Agni, the householder, has been proclaimed...'

12.9.99.s: athainaṃ yajamānāyatane tiṣṭhantaṃ prāha | eṣa vo bharatā rāja | iti yeṣām̐ śreṣṭhī bhavati
12.9.99.d: अथैनं यजमानायतने तिष्ठन्तं प्राह । एष वो भरता राज । इति येषाँ श्रेष्ठी भवति
12.9.99.m: Then he addresses him as he stands in the sacrificer's place: 'This is your king, O Bharatas!'—[inserting the name of those] of whom he is the leader.

12.9.99.s: somo 'smākaṃ brāhmaṇānām̐ rājā | itītare pratyāhus | athāsmai dhanuḥ prayacchati | indrasya vajro 'si vārtraghnas tvayāyaṃ vṛtraṃ vadhyāt | iti śatrubādhanā stha | itīṣūn |
12.9.99.d: सोमो ऽस्माकं ब्राह्मणानाँ राजा । इतीतरे प्रत्याहुस् । अथास्मै धनुः प्रयच्छति । इन्द्रस्य वज्रो ऽसि वार्त्रघ्नस् त्वयायं वृत्रं वध्यात् । इति शत्रुबाधना स्थ । इतीषून् ।
12.9.99.m: 'Soma is the king of us brāhmaṇas,' the others reply. Then he hands him a bow with: 'You are Indra's vajra, slayer of Vṛtra; through you may he slay Vṛtra!' and the arrows with: 'You are dispellers of foes!'

12.9.100.s: śatrūn me bādhadhvam itītaraḥ pratigṛhṇāti pāta mā pratyañcam | pāta mā tiryañcam anvañcaṃ mā pāta digbhyo mā pāta viśvābhyo mā nāṣṭrābhyaḥ pāta | iti |
12.9.100.d: शत्रून् मे बाधध्वम् इतीतरः प्रतिगृह्णाति पात मा प्रत्यञ्चम् । पात मा तिर्यञ्चम् अन्वञ्चं मा पात दिग्भ्यो मा पात विश्वाभ्यो मा नाष्ट्राभ्यः पात । इति ।
12.9.100.m: 'Dispel my foes!' the other accepts them with: 'Protect me against one coming from the west! Protect me against one coming from the side! Protect me against one coming from behind! Protect me against the quarters! Protect me from all perils!'

12.9.100.s: atha hiraṇyavarṇāv uṣasām̐ viroke | iti triṣṭubhā bāhū udgṛhṇāti |
12.9.100.d: अथ हिरण्यवर्णाव् उषसाँ विरोके । इति त्रिष्टुभा बाहू उद्गृह्णाति ।
12.9.100.m: Then with the triṣṭubh verse, 'Golden-hued at the dawn's flashing...', he raises his arms.

12.9.100.s: athainam̐ sam̐śāsti manasaiva diśo 'nuprakrāma manasordhvām anūjjihīṣva | iti |
12.9.100.d: अथैनँ सँशास्ति मनसैव दिशो ऽनुप्रक्राम मनसोर्ध्वाम् अनूज्जिहीष्व । इति ।
12.9.100.m: Then he instructs him: 'Stride through the quarters in mind alone; ascend upwards in mind alone.'

12.10.100.s: samidham ā tiṣṭha | ugrām ātiṣṭha virājam ā tiṣṭha | udīcīm ā tiṣṭha | ūrdhvām ā tiṣṭha | iti |
12.10.100.d: समिधम् आ तिष्ठ । उग्राम् आतिष्ठ विराजम् आ तिष्ठ । उदीचीम् आ तिष्ठ । ऊर्ध्वाम् आ तिष्ठ । इति ।
12.10.100.m: 'Ascend the Samidh! Ascend the Ugrā! Ascend the Virāj! Ascend the Udīcī! Ascend the Ūrdhvā!'

12.10.100.s: athātraiva tiṣṭhan yācati mārutaṃ caikavimśatikapālaṃ vaiśvadevīṃ cāmikṣām |
12.10.100.d: अथात्रैव तिष्ठन् याचति मारुतं चैकविम्शतिकपालं वैश्वदेवीं चामिक्षाम् ।
12.10.100.m: Then, standing right there, he asks for [the cake] on twenty-one potsherds for the Maruts and the curds for the All-gods.

12.10.100.s: tasya yo 'raṇye 'nuvākyo gaṇas tena madhyamāni kapālāny upahitāni bhavanti rājasūyagaṇābhyām itarāṇi
12.10.100.d: तस्य यो ऽरण्ये ऽनुवाक्यो गणस् तेन मध्यमानि कपालान्य् उपहितानि भवन्ति राजसूयगणाभ्याम् इतराणि
12.10.100.m: The potsherds in the middle are set down with that group which is the forest recitation; the others with the two groups of the Rājasūya.

12.10.100.s: tābhyāṃ carati marudbhyo 'nubrūhi maruto yaja | iti viśvebhyo devebhyo 'nubrūhi viśvān devān yaja | iti |
12.10.100.d: ताभ्यां चरति मरुद्भ्यो ऽनुब्रूहि मरुतो यज । इति विश्वेभ्यो देवेभ्यो ऽनुब्रूहि विश्वान् देवान् यज । इति ।
12.10.100.m: He proceeds with those two [oblations], with: 'Recite for the Maruts,' 'Sacrifice to the Maruts,' [and] 'Recite for the All-gods,' 'Sacrifice to the All-gods.'

12.10.100.s: aniṣṭasviṣṭakṛte evaite haviṣī apidhāya prajñāte nidadhāti |
12.10.100.d: अनिष्टस्विष्टकृते एवैते हविषी अपिधाय प्रज्ञाते निदधाति ।
12.10.100.m: Having covered these two oblations whose Sviṣṭakṛt offerings have not yet been performed, he places them in a known place.

12.10.100.s: atha yācati śārdūlacarma suvarṇarajatau ca rukmau vārāhī upānahau sīsaṃ ca lohitāyasaṃ ca
12.10.100.d: अथ याचति शार्दूलचर्म सुवर्णरजतौ च रुक्मौ वाराही उपानहौ सीसं च लोहितायसं च
12.10.100.m: Then he asks for a tiger skin, two gold and silver ornaments, two boar-skin sandals, lead, and copper.

12.10.101.s: dakṣiṇataḥ klība āste | atha purastād abhiṣekasya ṣaṭ pārthāni juhoti | agnaye svāhā somāya svāhā | iti |
12.10.101.d: दक्षिणतः क्लीब आस्ते । अथ पुरस्ताद् अभिषेकस्य षट् पार्थानि जुहोति । अग्नये स्वाहा सोमाय स्वाहा । इति ।
12.10.101.m: To the south sits a eunuch. Then, before the unction, he offers six Pārtha libations with: 'To Agni, svāhā! To Soma, svāhā!'

12.10.101.s: atha yajamānāyatane śārdūlacarma prācīnagrīvam uttaralomopastṛṇāti somasya tviṣir asi taveva me tviṣir bhūyāt | iti
12.10.101.d: अथ यजमानायतने शार्दूलचर्म प्राचीनग्रीवम् उत्तरलोमोपस्तृणाति सोमस्य त्विषिर् असि तवेव मे त्विषिर् भूयात् । इति
12.10.101.m: Then in the sacrificer's place he spreads out the tiger skin, with its neck to the east and its fur upward, with: 'You are the splendor of Soma; may my splendor be like yours.'

12.10.101.s: tad yajamānaṃ prāñcam upaveśya suvarṇarajatābhyām̐ rukmābhyāṃ paryupāsyati |
12.10.101.d: तद् यजमानं प्राञ्चम् उपवेश्य सुवर्णरजताभ्याँ रुक्माभ्यां पर्युपास्यति ।
12.10.101.m: Having seated the sacrificer facing east upon it, he surrounds him with the two gold and silver ornaments.

12.10.101.s: amṛtam asi mṛtyor mā pāhi | ity adhastād rajatam upāsyati didyon mā pāhi | ity upariṣṭāt suvarṇam̐ śatātṛṇṇam
12.10.101.d: अमृतम् असि मृत्योर् मा पाहि । इत्य् अधस्ताद् रजतम् उपास्यति दिद्योन् मा पाहि । इत्य् उपरिष्टात् सुवर्णँ शतातृण्णम्
12.10.101.m: With 'You are immortal; protect me from death,' he lays the silver one underneath; with 'Protect me from the lightning flash,' [he lays] the perforated gold one above.

12.10.101.s: atha | aveṣṭā dandaśūkās | iti dakṣiṇata āsīnaṃ klībam̐ sīsena vidhyati
12.10.101.d: अथ । अवेष्टा दन्दशूकास् । इति दक्षिणत आसीनं क्लीबँ सीसेन विध्यति
12.10.101.m: Then with 'The biting [creatures] are driven away,' he pierces the eunuch sitting to the south with the lead.

12.10.101.s: savyena pādena lohitāyasaṃ nirasyati nirastaṃ namuceḥ śiras | iti |
12.10.101.d: सव्येन पादेन लोहितायसं निरस्यति निरस्तं नमुचेः शिरस् । इति ।
12.10.101.m: With his left foot he casts away the copper with: 'Cast away is the head of Namuci.'
At this point, they take up the unction-waters for him.

12.11.101.s: somo rājā varuṇo devā dharmasuvaś ca ye | te te vācam̐ suvantām | te te prāṇam̐ suvantām | te te cakṣuḥ suvantām | te te śrotram̐ suvantām iti |
12.11.101.d: सोमो राजा वरुणो देवा धर्मसुवश् च ये । ते ते वाचँ सुवन्ताम् । ते ते प्राणँ सुवन्ताम् । ते ते चक्षुः सुवन्ताम् । ते ते श्रोत्रँ सुवन्ताम् इति ।
12.11.101.m: 'King Soma, Varuṇa, and the gods that promote sacred order: may they quicken your speech, may they quicken your breath, may they quicken your eye, may they quicken your ear!'

12.11.101.s: atha brahmaṇaḥ pātram ādāya tenābhiṣiñcati | adhvaryur eva yajur japaty abhiṣiñcantītare somasya tvā dyumnenābhiṣiñcāmy agnes tejasā sūryasya varcasendrasyendriyeṇa mitrāvaruṇayor vīryeṇa marutām ojasā kṣatrāṇāṃ kṣatrapatir asi | ati divas pāhy asau | iti |
12.11.101.d: अथ ब्रह्मणः पात्रम् आदाय तेनाभिषिञ्चति । अध्वर्युर् एव यजुर् जपत्य् अभिषिञ्चन्तीतरे सोमस्य त्वा द्युम्नेनाभिषिञ्चाम्य् अग्नेस् तेजसा सूर्यस्य वर्चसेन्द्रस्येन्द्रियेण मित्रावरुणयोर् वीर्येण मरुताम् ओजसा क्षत्राणां क्षत्रपतिर् असि । अति दिवस् पाह्य् असौ । इति ।
12.11.101.m: Then, taking the vessel of the brahman priest, he consecrates him with it. The adhvaryu priest simply mutters the formula while the others consecrate him with: 'With the brightness of Soma I consecrate you, with the luster of Agni, with the brilliance of Sūrya, with the faculty of Indra, with the valor of Mitra and Varuṇa, with the might of the Maruts! You are the lord of dominion among rulers! Protect [us] beyond heaven, O so-and-so!'

12.11.101.s: athordhvā dhārāḥ samunmṛṣṭe samāvavṛtrann adharāg udīcīs | ahiṃ budhniyam anu saṃcarantīs tāḥ parvatasya vṛṣabhasya pṛṣṭhe nāvaś caranti svasica iyānās | iti |
12.11.101.d: अथोर्ध्वा धाराः समुन्मृष्टे समाववृत्रन्न् अधराग् उदीचीस् । अहिं बुध्नियम् अनु संचरन्तीस् ताः पर्वतस्य वृषभस्य पृष्ठे नावश् चरन्ति स्वसिच इयानास् । इति ।
12.11.101.m: Then he wipes upward the streams of water with: 'Turning downward and northward, moving toward Ahi Budhnya, like ships on the back of the mountain bull, flowing freely, moving along.'

12.11.102.s: atraiteṣām abhiṣekāṇāṃ mukhye pātre sam̐srāvān samavanīya pratihitasya gṛhān eti |
12.11.102.d: अत्रैतेषाम् अभिषेकाणां मुख्ये पात्रे सँस्रावान् समवनीय प्रतिहितस्य गृहान् एति ।
12.11.102.m: At this point, having poured together the residues of these unction-waters into the principal vessel, he goes to the house of the king's rival.

12.11.102.s: athānvārabdhayoḥ pratihite ca mahiṣyāṃ ca juhoti prajāpate na tvad etāny anyas | iti |
12.11.102.d: अथान्वारब्धयोः प्रतिहिते च महिष्यां च जुहोति प्रजापते न त्वद् एतान्य् अन्यस् । इति ।
12.11.102.m: Then, while the rival and the chief queen are touching [him] from behind, he makes an offering with: 'O Prajāpati, none other than you [has encompassed all these forms]...'
At this point, this rival gives him a boon.

12.11.102.s: atha pratihitāya pātraṃ prayacchann āha | idaṃ te pātraṃ dāyād yam asad yadā tvābhiṣiñcāmīdaṃ te 'sat | iti |
12.11.102.d: अथ प्रतिहिताय पात्रं प्रयच्छन्न् आह । इदं ते पात्रं दायाद् यम् असद् यदा त्वाभिषिञ्चामीदं ते ऽसत् । इति ।
12.11.102.m: Then, handing the vessel to the rival, he says: 'This vessel shall be your inheritance; when I consecrate you, this shall be yours.'

12.11.102.s: athaitenaiva yathetam etyāgnīdhre prarekaṃ juhoti rudra yat te krayī paraṃ nāma tasmai hutam asi yameṣṭam asi svāhā | iti |
12.11.102.d: अथैतेनैव यथेतम् एत्याग्नीध्रे प्ररेकं जुहोति रुद्र यत् ते क्रयी परं नाम तस्मै हुतम् असि यमेष्टम् असि स्वाहा । इति ।
12.11.102.m: Then, returning along the same path by which he had gone, he offers the residue in the āgnīdhra [fire] with: 'O Rudra, to that supreme name of yours, the buyer, this is offered; it is acceptable to Yama, svāhā!'

12.11.102.s: atrāsmai dhanuḥ prayacchati yadi purastād aprattaṃ bhavati
12.11.102.d: अत्रास्मै धनुः प्रयच्छति यदि पुरस्ताद् अप्रत्तं भवति
12.11.102.m: At this point, he hands him the bow, if it was not given earlier.

12.11.102.s: samunmṛṣṭe samutkrośanti | abhyaṣecy ayam asāv āmuṣyāyaṇo 'muṣya putro 'muṣya pautro 'muṣya naptā rājasūyena | iti |
12.11.102.d: समुन्मृष्टे समुत्क्रोशन्ति । अभ्यषेच्य् अयम् असाव् आमुष्यायणो ऽमुष्य पुत्रो ऽमुष्य पौत्रो ऽमुष्य नप्ता राजसूयेन । इति ।
12.11.102.m: When [the moisture] has been wiped off, they proclaim aloud: 'This so-and-so, of such-and-such lineage, son of so-and-so, grandson of so-and-so, great-grandson of so-and-so, has been consecrated through the Rājasūya!'

12.11.102.s: atha bhūr bhuvaḥ suvar iti vācaṃ visṛjate
12.11.102.d: अथ भूर् भुवः सुवर् इति वाचं विसृजते
12.11.102.m: Then he releases his speech with: 'Bhūr, bhuvaḥ, suvar!'

12.11.102.s: dvābhyāṃ mukhaṃ vimṛṣṭe gāyatrān viṣṇukramān kramate |
12.11.102.d: द्वाभ्यां मुखं विमृष्टे गायत्रान् विष्णुक्रमान् क्रमते ।
12.11.102.m: He wipes his face with two [verses]. He strides the Viṣṇu-strides in the gāyatrī meter.

12.11.102.s: athopariṣṭād abhiṣekasya ṣaṭ pārthāni juhoti | indrāya svāhā ghoṣāya svāhā | iti
12.11.102.d: अथोपरिष्टाद् अभिषेकस्य षट् पार्थानि जुहोति । इन्द्राय स्वाहा घोषाय स्वाहा । इति
12.11.102.m: Then, after the unction, he offers the six Pārtha libations with: 'To Indra, svāhā! To Ghoṣa, svāhā!'

12.11.102.s: dvādaśa bhūtānām aveṣṭīr juhoti pṛthivyai svāhāntarikṣāya svāhā | iti |
12.11.102.d: द्वादश भूतानाम् अवेष्टीर् जुहोति पृथिव्यै स्वाहान्तरिक्षाय स्वाहा । इति ।
12.11.102.m: He offers twelve Aveṣṭi libations to the beings with: 'To the earth, svāhā! To the intermediate space, svāhā!'
At this point, he proceeds with the Sviṣṭakṛt offering of these two oblations.
Then, having covered the two, he places them in a known place.

12.12.102.s: atha vārāho upānahāv upamuñcate paśūnāṃ manyur asi | iti dakṣiṇe pāde taveva me manyur bhūyāt | iti savye |
12.12.102.d: अथ वाराहो उपानहाव् उपमुञ्चते पशूनां मन्युर् असि । इति दक्षिणे पादे तवेव मे मन्युर् भूयात् । इति सव्ये ।
12.12.102.m: Then he puts on the two boar-skin sandals with 'You are the wrath of beasts' on the right foot, and 'May my wrath be like yours' on the left.

12.12.103.s: athemām abhimṛśati namo mātre pṛthivyai | iti
12.12.103.d: अथेमाम् अभिमृशति नमो मात्रे पृथिव्यै । इति
12.12.103.m: Then he touches this [earth] with: 'Homage to Mother Earth!'

12.12.103.s: tasyāṃ dakṣiṇaṃ pādam upāvaharati māhaṃ mātaraṃ pṛthivīm̐ sim̐siṣam iti mā māṃ mātā pṛthivī him̐sīt | iti savyam
12.12.103.d: तस्यां दक्षिणं पादम् उपावहरति माहं मातरं पृथिवीँ सिँसिषम् इति मा मां माता पृथिवी हिँसीत् । इति सव्यम्
12.12.103.m: He puts his right foot down upon it with 'May I not harm Mother Earth,' and his left with 'May Mother Earth not harm me.'

12.12.103.s: athāntareṇa cātvālotkarāv udaṅṅ upaniṣkrāmati viṣṇoḥ kramo 'si viṣṇoḥ krāntam asi viṣṇor vikrāntam asi | iti |
12.12.103.d: अथान्तरेण चात्वालोत्कराव् उदङ्ङ् उपनिष्क्रामति विष्णोः क्रमो ऽसि विष्णोः क्रान्तम् असि विष्णोर् विक्रान्तम् असि । इति ।
12.12.103.m: Then he steps out northward between the pit and the rubbish heap with: 'You are the stride of Viṣṇu; you are the stepped stride of Viṣṇu; you are the wide step of Viṣṇu.'

12.12.103.s: uttarata ete rathā yuktās tiṣṭhanti tān dṛṣṭvaiva pratihito 'vatiṣṭhati |
12.12.103.d: उत्तरत एते रथा युक्तास् तिष्ठन्ति तान् दृष्ट्वैव प्रतिहितो ऽवतिष्ठति ।
12.12.103.m: To the north, these chariots stand yoked. Having seen them, the rival steps down.

12.12.103.s: atha pratihitasya dhanur ādāyādhijyaṃ kṛtvā ratham ātiṣṭhati marutāṃ prasave jeṣam iti |
12.12.103.d: अथ प्रतिहितस्य धनुर् आदायाधिज्यं कृत्वा रथम् आतिष्ठति मरुतां प्रसवे जेषम् इति ।
12.12.103.m: Then, taking the bow of the rival and stringing it, he mounts the chariot with: 'May I conquer under the impulse of the Maruts!'
With: 'The mind is attained,' he leans against the pole.

12.12.103.s: taṃ tadānīm eva pratihito 'nvātiṣṭhati prasasāhiṣe puruhūta śatrūn iti
12.12.103.d: तं तदानीम् एव प्रतिहितो ऽन्वातिष्ठति प्रससाहिषे पुरुहूत शत्रून् इति
12.12.103.m: At that very moment, the representative mounts behind him, with: 'You have conquered the enemies, O much-invoked one!'

12.12.103.s: triṣṭubhānvārabhate | iti brāhmaṇam atha pratihitāya dhanuḥ prayacchann āha rājanya eṣa ṣaṭtrim̐śatsu śamyāpravyādheṣu nirjayena sahasreṇāvasitas tasmā iṣum asyatād apainam̐ rādhnutāj jitvainaṃ dakṣiṇāpathenātyākurutāt | iti
12.12.103.d: त्रिष्टुभान्वारभते । इति ब्राह्मणम् अथ प्रतिहिताय धनुः प्रयच्छन्न् आह राजन्य एष षट्त्रिँशत्सु शम्याप्रव्याधेषु निर्जयेन सहस्रेणावसितस् तस्मा इषुम् अस्यताद् अपैनँ राध्नुताज् जित्वैनं दक्षिणापथेनात्याकुरुतात् । इति
12.12.103.m: 'He takes hold from behind with a triṣṭubh verse,' says the brāhmaṇa passage. Then, handing the bow to the representative, he says: 'This noble, who has settled at thirty-six yoke-pin throws with a conquered thousand—shoot an arrow at him; overcome him; having defeated him, drive past him along the southern path.'

12.12.103.s: rājanya eva sam̐śiṣṭo bhavati rājaputras ta iṣum asiṣyati sa tvāparātsyati tasmā uttaravargyeṇa saṃmṛjyeṣu prayacchatāt | iti
12.12.103.d: राजन्य एव सँशिष्टो भवति राजपुत्रस् त इषुम् असिष्यति स त्वापरात्स्यति तस्मा उत्तरवर्ग्येण संमृज्येषु प्रयच्छतात् । इति
12.12.103.m: The noble has already been instructed: 'The prince will shoot an arrow at you; he will miss you; having wiped the arrow with the subsequent hem of your garment, hand it back to him.'

12.13.104.s: athāha | abhisarpa yajamāna māhendraṃ grahaṃ grahīṣyāmi | iti | anvārabdhe yajamāne māhendraṃ grahaṃ gṛhṇāti mahām̐ indro ya ojasā | ity anudrutya | upayāmagṛhīto 'si mahendrāya tvā juṣṭaṃ gṛhṇāmi | iti
12.13.104.d: अथाह । अभिसर्प यजमान माहेन्द्रं ग्रहं ग्रहीष्यामि । इति । अन्वारब्धे यजमाने माहेन्द्रं ग्रहं गृह्णाति महाँ इन्द्रो य ओजसा । इत्य् अनुद्रुत्य । उपयामगृहीतो ऽसि महेन्द्राय त्वा जुष्टं गृह्णामि । इति
12.13.104.m: Then he says: 'Approach, O sacrificer; I shall draw the Māhendra soma-cup.' When the sacrificer has touched him from behind, he draws the Māhendra soma-cup, reciting: 'Great is Indra, who through his power,' [and adds:] 'You are taken with a support; I draw you, pleasing to Mahendra.'

12.13.104.s: parimṛjya sādayati | eṣa te yonir mahendrāya tvā | iti |
12.13.104.d: परिमृज्य सादयति । एष ते योनिर् महेन्द्राय त्वा । इति ।
12.13.104.m: Having wiped it around, he sets it down with: 'This is your womb; for Mahendra you.'

12.13.104.s: athaitān maṇīn yācati rājatam audumbaram̐ sauvarṇam iti
12.13.104.d: अथैतान् मणीन् याचति राजतम् औदुम्बरँ सौवर्णम् इति
12.13.104.m: Then he asks for these beads: of silver, of udumbara wood, and of gold.
They are strung on different threads.

12.13.104.s: tān uttarasya havirdhānasya madhyame vam̐śe pragrathyāpa upaspṛśya barhiṣī ādāya vācaṃyamaḥ pratyaṅ drutvā stotram upākaroti
12.13.104.d: तान् उत्तरस्य हविर्धानस्य मध्यमे वँशे प्रग्रथ्याप उपस्पृश्य बर्हिषी आदाय वाचंयमः प्रत्यङ् द्रुत्वा स्तोत्रम् उपाकरोति
12.13.104.m: Having tied them to the middle beam of the northern havirdhāna shed, having touched water, and having taken two stalks of sacrificial grass, keeping silence, he runs west and introduces the chant.

12.13.104.s: stuvate māhendrāya prastute sāmni saṃpraiṣam āha | ājisṛta ājiṃ dhāvata dundubhīn samāghnata | abhiṣotāro 'bhiṣuṇuta | agnīd āśiraṃ vinayolūkhalam udvādaya pratiprasthātar vāruṇam ekakapālaṃ nirvapa saumyasya viddhi | iti
12.13.104.d: स्तुवते माहेन्द्राय प्रस्तुते साम्नि संप्रैषम् आह । आजिसृत आजिं धावत दुन्दुभीन् समाघ्नत । अभिषोतारो ऽभिषुणुत । अग्नीद् आशिरं विनयोलूखलम् उद्वादय प्रतिप्रस्थातर् वारुणम् एककपालं निर्वप सौम्यस्य विद्धि । इति
12.13.104.m: They chant for the Māhendra cup. While the sāman is being chanted, he issues the directions: 'Runners of the race, run the race! Beat the drums together! Pressers, press [the soma]! Agnīdh, pour in the warm milk, make the mortar resound! Pratiprasthātṛ priest, prepare the one-potsherd cake for Varuṇa; pay attention to the Soma offering!'

12.13.105.m: They act according to the directions. The runners run the race.

12.13.105.s: āghnanti dundubhīn saṃpravadanti vācaḥ saṃproditā vāco 'numantrayate
12.13.105.d: आघ्नन्ति दुन्दुभीन् संप्रवदन्ति वाचः संप्रोदिता वाचो ऽनुमन्त्रयते
12.13.105.m: They beat the drums. Voices sound together. He follows the voices sounding together with a recitation.

12.13.105.s: śāmyanti ghoṣāḥ śastrāya hotre | eṣottamā | iti prāhus |
12.13.105.d: शाम्यन्ति घोषाः शस्त्राय होत्रे । एषोत्तमा । इति प्राहुस् ।
12.13.105.m: The sounds quiet down for the recitation. They say to the hotṛ priest: 'This is the last verse.'

12.13.105.s: hotuḥ kālāt parāṅ āvartate 'dhvaryus | abhy enam āhvayate hotā pratyāhvayate 'dhvaryuḥ
12.13.105.d: होतुः कालात् पराङ् आवर्तते ऽध्वर्युस् । अभ्य् एनम् आह्वयते होता प्रत्याह्वयते ऽध्वर्युः
12.13.105.m: At the signal of the hotṛ priest, the adhvaryu priest turns away. The hotṛ priest addresses him; the adhvaryu priest replies.

12.13.105.s: śam̐sati pratigṛṇāti prasiddham ukthaṃ pratigīrya prāṅ etyodyacchat etaṃ māhendraṃ graham
12.13.105.d: शँसति प्रतिगृणाति प्रसिद्धम् उक्थं प्रतिगीर्य प्राङ् एत्योद्यच्छत् एतं माहेन्द्रं ग्रहम्
12.13.105.m: He recites. He utters the response. Having responded to the uktha in the prescribed manner, he goes east and holds aloft this Māhendra soma-cup.
They hold aloft the other [cups] after [it]; they hold aloft the nārāśaṃsa cups nearby.

12.13.105.s: athāśrāvayati | o śrāvaya | astu śrauṣaṭ | ukthaśā yaja somasya | iti
12.13.105.d: अथाश्रावयति । ओ श्रावय । अस्तु श्रौषट् । उक्थशा यज सोमस्य । इति
12.13.105.m: Then he makes the call: 'Call!' — 'Let there be hearing!' — 'Reciter of the uktha, recite for the soma.'

12.13.105.s: vaṣaṭkṛtānuvaṣaṭkṛte dvir juhoti tathaiva dvirdvir nārāśam̐sānam upakampayanti
12.13.105.d: वषट्कृतानुवषट्कृते द्विर् जुहोति तथैव द्विर्द्विर् नाराशँसानम् उपकम्पयन्ति
12.13.105.m: Upon the vaṣaṭ call and the second vaṣaṭ call, he offers twice. Just so, they shake the nārāśaṃsa cups twice each.
Offered twice, the Māhendra cup lies aside.

12.13.105.s: āyanti rathās | āgatān rathān dṛṣṭvā japati sam aham indriyeṇa vīryeṇa saṃ mayendriyaṃ vīryam iti
12.13.105.d: आयन्ति रथास् । आगतान् रथान् दृष्ट्वा जपति सम् अहम् इन्द्रियेण वीर्येण सं मयेन्द्रियं वीर्यम् इति
12.13.105.m: The chariots arrive. Seeing the chariots arrived, he murmurs: 'I unite with faculty and strength; may faculty and strength unite in me.'
Then he steps out northward between the pit and the rubbish heap.

12.13.105.s: uttarata ete rathā yuktās tiṣṭhanti tān dṛṣṭvaiva pratihito 'vatiṣṭhati |
12.13.105.d: उत्तरत एते रथा युक्तास् तिष्ठन्ति तान् दृष्ट्वैव प्रतिहितो ऽवतिष्ठति ।
12.13.105.m: In the north, these chariots stand yoked. Merely seeing them, the representative steps down.

12.13.105.s: atha pratihitasya dhanur ādāyādhijyaṃ kṛtvā ratham ātiṣṭhati marutāṃ prasave jeṣam iti |
12.13.105.d: अथ प्रतिहितस्य धनुर् आदायाधिज्यं कृत्वा रथम् आतिष्ठति मरुतां प्रसवे जेषम् इति ।
12.13.105.m: Then, having taken the representative's bow and strung it, he mounts the chariot with: 'At the instigation of the Maruts may I conquer.'
With: 'The mind is attained,' he leans against the pole.

12.13.106.s: taṃ tadānīm eva pratihito 'nvātiṣṭhati prasasāhiṣe puruhūta śatrūn iti
12.13.106.d: तं तदानीम् एव प्रतिहितो ऽन्वातिष्ठति प्रससाहिषे पुरुहूत शत्रून् इति
12.13.106.m: At that very moment, the representative mounts behind him, with: 'You have conquered the enemies, O much-invoked one!'

12.13.106.s: triṣṭubhānvārabhate | iti brāhmaṇam atha pratihitāya dhanuḥ prayacchann āha | idaṃ te dhanur dāyād yam asad yadā tvābhiṣiñcāmīdaṃ te 'sat | iti |
12.13.106.d: त्रिष्टुभान्वारभते । इति ब्राह्मणम् अथ प्रतिहिताय धनुः प्रयच्छन्न् आह । इदं ते धनुर् दायाद् यम् असद् यदा त्वाभिषिञ्चामीदं ते ऽसत् । इति ।
12.13.106.m: 'He takes hold from behind with a triṣṭubh verse,' says the brāhmaṇa passage. Then, handing the bow to the representative, he says: 'This bow is yours, which will be the heir's; when I consecrate you, this shall be yours.'

12.13.106.s: athaitenaiva yathetam etyāntareṇa cātvālotkarāv upātītya pūrvayā dvārā havirdhānaṃ prapādya prāñcam̐ ratham āvartya tiṣṭhati ||
12.13.106.d: अथैतेनैव यथेतम् एत्यान्तरेण चात्वालोत्कराव् उपातीत्य पूर्वया द्वारा हविर्धानं प्रपाद्य प्राञ्चँ रथम् आवर्त्य तिष्ठति ॥
12.13.106.m: Then, returning by the very way he went, passing between the pit and the rubbish heap, entering the havirdhāna shed by the eastern door, and turning the chariot eastward, he remains.

12.14.106.s: tad etān maṇīn yācati rājatam audumbaram̐ sauvarṇam iti savye haste rājataṃ pratimuñcate | iyad asyāyur asy āyur me dhehi | iti dakṣiṇa audumbaram ūrg asy ūrjaṃ me dhehi | iti dakṣiṇa eva sauvarṇaṃ yuṅṅ asi varco 'si varco mayi dhehi | iti |
12.14.106.d: तद् एतान् मणीन् याचति राजतम् औदुम्बरँ सौवर्णम् इति सव्ये हस्ते राजतं प्रतिमुञ्चते । इयद् अस्यायुर् अस्य् आयुर् मे धेहि । इति दक्षिण औदुम्बरम् ऊर्ग् अस्य् ऊर्जं मे धेहि । इति दक्षिण एव सौवर्णं युङ्ङ् असि वर्चो ऽसि वर्चो मयि धेहि । इति ।
12.14.106.m: Then he asks for these beads: of silver, of udumbara wood, and of gold. He fastens the silver one on the left hand with: 'So much you are; you are life, bestow life upon me'; the udumbara one on the right with: 'You are vigor, bestow vigor upon me'; and the gold one on the right itself with: 'You are linked; you are brilliance, bestow brilliance in me.'

12.14.106.s: atrāsmā āmikṣām upodyacchate tasyāṃ dakṣiṇam̐ hastam upāvaharati mitro 'si | iti varuṇo 'si | iti savyam
12.14.106.d: अत्रास्मा आमिक्षाम् उपोद्यच्छते तस्यां दक्षिणँ हस्तम् उपावहरति मित्रो ऽसि । इति वरुणो ऽसि । इति सव्यम्
12.14.106.m: Here they hold up the clotted curds to him. Over it, he lowers his right hand with: 'You are Mitra,' and his left with: 'You are Varuṇa.'

12.14.106.s: athainām abhimṛśati sam ahaṃ viśvair devais | iti | athainām apidhāya prajñātāṃ nidadhāti
12.14.106.d: अथैनाम् अभिमृशति सम् अहं विश्वैर् देवैस् । इति । अथैनाम् अपिधाय प्रज्ञातां निदधाति
12.14.106.m: Then he touches it with: 'Together with all the gods, I...'; then, covering it, he puts it down in a recognized place.

12.14.106.s: tad etān maṇīn ekasmin sūtra āvayati madhyata audumbaraṃ karoti
12.14.106.d: तद् एतान् मणीन् एकस्मिन् सूत्र आवयति मध्यत औदुम्बरं करोति
12.14.106.m: Then he strings these beads on a single cord; he places the udumbara one in the middle.

12.14.106.s: tān grīvāsu pratiṣajyaitenaiva yathetam etyāgreṇāgnīdhraṃ prāñcam̐ ratham āvartyāvatiṣṭhati |
12.14.106.d: तान् ग्रीवासु प्रतिषज्यैतेनैव यथेतम् एत्याग्रेणाग्नीध्रं प्राञ्चँ रथम् आवर्त्यावतिष्ठति ।
12.14.106.m: Having fastened them around his neck, returning by the very way he went, turning the chariot eastward in front of the āgnīdhra shed, he halts.

12.14.107.s: athāgnīdhre rathavimocanīyā juhoti | agnaye gṛhapataye svāhā | iti catasraḥ sruvāhutīs |
12.14.107.d: अथाग्नीध्रे रथविमोचनीया जुहोति । अग्नये गृहपतये स्वाहा । इति चतस्रः स्रुवाहुतीस् ।
12.14.107.m: Then in the āgnīdhra shed he offers the chariot-unyoking libations: 'To Agni, lord of the house, svāhā,' making four ladle libations.

12.14.107.s: athāsyaitat purastād evāgreṇāgnīdhram̐ rathavāhanaṃ prāgīṣaṃ yogyakṛtam upasthitaṃ bhavati
12.14.107.d: अथास्यैतत् पुरस्ताद् एवाग्रेणाग्नीध्रँ रथवाहनं प्रागीषं योग्यकृतम् उपस्थितं भवति
12.14.107.m: Now beforehand, in front of the āgnīdhra shed, a chariot-stand with its pole facing east and made fit for yoking has already been placed for him.

12.14.107.s: tasmin saha saṃgrahītrā rathavāhane ratham ādadhāti
12.14.107.d: तस्मिन् सह संग्रहीत्रा रथवाहने रथम् आदधाति
12.14.107.m: On that chariot-stand, together with the charioteer, he places the chariot.

12.14.107.s: suvargād evainaṃ lokād antardadhāti ham̐saḥ śuciṣad | ity ādadhāti
12.14.107.d: सुवर्गाद् एवैनं लोकाद् अन्तर्दधाति हँसः शुचिषद् । इत्य् आदधाति
12.14.107.m: He conceals him from the heavenly world. With: 'The goose seated in the light,' he places it.

12.14.107.s: brahmaṇaivainam upāvaharati brahmaṇādadhāti | aticchandasādadhāti | iti brāhmaṇam
12.14.107.d: ब्रह्मणैवैनम् उपावहरति ब्रह्मणादधाति । अतिच्छन्दसादधाति । इति ब्राह्मणम्
12.14.107.m: With sacred power he lowers it; with sacred power he places it. 'He places it with an aticchandas verse,' says the brāhmaṇa passage.

12.14.107.s: athāsyaitat purastād eva jaghanenāgrīdhraṃ caturapasrāvaṃ vāṣṭāpasrāvaṃ vā vimitaṃ kāritaṃ bhavati
12.14.107.d: अथास्यैतत् पुरस्ताद् एव जघनेनाग्रीध्रं चतुरपस्रावं वाष्टापस्रावं वा विमितं कारितं भवति
12.14.107.m: Now beforehand, behind the āgnīdhra shed, a four-roofed or eight-roofed shed has been made for him.

12.14.107.s: tasya madhyata audumbarīm āsandīṃ niminoti kṣatrasya nābhir asi | iti
12.14.107.d: तस्य मध्यत औदुम्बरीम् आसन्दीं निमिनोति क्षत्रस्य नाभिर् असि । इति
12.14.107.m: In the middle of it he sets up an audumbarī seat with: 'You are the navel of royal power.'

12.14.107.s: tasyām uttaramaṣṭanam adhīvāsam āstṛṇāti kṣatrasya yonir asi | iti |
12.14.107.d: तस्याम् उत्तरमष्टनम् अधीवासम् आस्तृणाति क्षत्रस्य योनिर् असि । इति ।
12.14.107.m: On it he spreads an outer cloak of eight [thicknesses] with: 'You are the womb of royal power.'

12.14.107.s: athainām āsīdati | āsīdantam anumantrayate syonām āsīda suṣadām āsīda mā tvā him̐sīt | iti
12.14.107.d: अथैनाम् आसीदति । आसीदन्तम् अनुमन्त्रयते स्योनाम् आसीद सुषदाम् आसीद मा त्वा हिँसीत् । इति
12.14.107.m: Then he sits down on it. As he sits down, he follows him with the formula: 'Sit on the pleasant, sit on the easy-to-sit; may it not harm you.'

12.14.107.s: mā mā him̐sīt | itītaraḥ pratyāha | āsannam abhimantrayate niṣasāda dhṛtavrato varuṇaḥ pastyāsv ā samrājyāya sukratus | iti |
12.14.107.d: मा मा हिँसीत् । इतीतरः प्रत्याह । आसन्नम् अभिमन्त्रयते निषसाद धृतव्रतो वरुणः पस्त्यास्व् आ सम्राज्याय सुक्रतुस् । इति ।
12.14.107.m: "May it not injure me," the other responds. Over him as he sits down, he recites: "Varuṇa, of firm resolve, has sat down among the dwellings, of noble power, for imperial sovereignty."

12.14.108.s: athainam ṛtvijaḥ paryupaviśanti purastād adhvaryur upaviśati dakṣiṇato brahmā paścād dhotodgātottaratas
12.14.108.d: अथैनम् ऋत्विजः पर्युपविशन्ति पुरस्ताद् अध्वर्युर् उपविशति दक्षिणतो ब्रह्मा पश्चाद् धोतोद्गातोत्तरतस्
12.14.108.m: Then the officiating priests sit around him: in front sits the adhvaryu priest, to the south the brahman priest, behind the hotṛ priest, and to the north the udgātṛ priest;
then, facing east or north, the royal attendants.

12.15.108.s: brahmā3n iti hotāram | tvam̐ rājan brahmāsi | ity āha hotā mitro 'si suśevas | iti
12.15.108.d: ब्रह्मा३न् इति होतारम् । त्वँ राजन् ब्रह्मासि । इत्य् आह होता मित्रो ऽसि सुशेवस् । इति
12.15.108.m: "O King, you are Brahman," says the adhvaryu priest, "you are Savitar, of true impulse."
"O King, you are Brahman," says the brahman priest, "you are Indra, of true power."

12.15.108.s: tvam̐ rājan brahmāsi | ity āhodgātā varuṇo 'si satyadharmā | iti
12.15.108.d: त्वँ राजन् ब्रह्मासि । इत्य् आहोद्गाता वरुणो ऽसि सत्यधर्मा । इति
12.15.108.m: "O King, you are Brahman," says the udgātṛ priest, "you are Varuṇa, of true law."

12.15.108.s: suślokā3m̐ suślokā3n iti kṣattāram | tvam̐ rājan suśloko 'si | ity āha kṣattā
12.15.108.d: सुश्लोका३ँ सुश्लोका३न् इति क्षत्तारम् । त्वँ राजन् सुश्लोको ऽसि । इत्य् आह क्षत्ता
12.15.108.m: "O one of good renown!" [he addresses] the chamberlain. "O King, you are of good renown," says the chamberlain.

12.15.108.s: sumaṅgalā3m̐ sumaṅgalā3n iti saṃgrahītāram | tvam̐ rajān sumaṅgalo 'si | ity āha saṃgrahītā
12.15.108.d: सुमङ्गला३ँ सुमङ्गला३न् इति संग्रहीतारम् । त्वँ रजान् सुमङ्गलो ऽसि । इत्य् आह संग्रहीता
12.15.108.m: "O very auspicious one!" [he addresses] the charioteer. "O King, you are very auspicious," says the charioteer.

12.15.108.s: tvam̐ rājan satyarājāsi | ity āha bhāgadhuk sapta puṇyanāmno 'bhyudyāthāsmai sphyaṃ prayacchati | indrasya vajro 'si vārtraghnas tena me radhya | iti
12.15.108.d: त्वँ राजन् सत्यराजासि । इत्य् आह भागधुक् सप्त पुण्यनाम्नो ऽभ्युद्याथास्मै स्फ्यं प्रयच्छति । इन्द्रस्य वज्रो ऽसि वार्त्रघ्नस् तेन मे रध्य । इति
12.15.108.m: "O King, you are a true king," says the tax-collector. Having addressed the seven with auspicious names, he then gives him the wooden sword: "You are Indra's thunderbolt, slayer of Vṛtra; through it, be subject to me."

12.15.108.s: tena te radhyāsam itītaraḥ pratigṛhṇāti tam̐ saṃprayacchati sūtāya sūtagrāmaṇine sajātāya sajātagrāmaṇine saṃgrahītre 'kṣāvāpagovyacchābhyām antatas
12.15.108.d: तेन ते रध्यासम् इतीतरः प्रतिगृह्णाति तँ संप्रयच्छति सूताय सूतग्रामणिने सजाताय सजातग्रामणिने संग्रहीत्रे ऽक्षावापगोव्यच्छाभ्याम् अन्ततस्
12.15.108.m: "Through it may I be subject to you," the other accepts it. He passes it to the herald, to the herald-headman, to the kinsman, to the kinsman-headman, to the charioteer, and finally to the dice-thrower and the cattle-checker.

12.15.108.s: tena tau madhyato 'dhidevanam uddhatya tisraḥ pañcāśataḥ sauvarṇān akṣān nivapatas |
12.15.108.d: तेन तौ मध्यतो ऽधिदेवनम् उद्धत्य तिस्रः पञ्चाशतः सौवर्णान् अक्षान् निवपतस् ।
12.15.108.m: With it, the two, having dug up a gambling place in the middle, scatter three times fifty golden dice.

12.15.109.s: athāsmai pañcākṣān apacchidya prayacchati diśo 'bhy ayam̐ rājābhūt | iti
12.15.109.d: अथास्मै पञ्चाक्षान् अपच्छिद्य प्रयच्छति दिशो ऽभ्य् अयँ राजाभूत् । इति
12.15.109.m: Then, taking off five dice, he hands them to him: "This king has overcome the quarters!"

12.15.109.s: tām̐s tadānīm evākṣeṣv apisṛjati | athaitam odanam udbruvate nānām̐śinau brahmā ca yajamānaś ca samānām̐śinau sūtagrāmaṇinau samānām̐śinau kṣattasaṃgrahītārau
12.15.109.d: ताँस् तदानीम् एवाक्षेष्व् अपिसृजति । अथैतम् ओदनम् उद्ब्रुवते नानाँशिनौ ब्रह्मा च यजमानश् च समानाँशिनौ सूतग्रामणिनौ समानाँशिनौ क्षत्तसंग्रहीतारौ
12.15.109.m: He immediately mixes them into the dice. Then they announce this rice mess: "The brahman priest and the sacrificer are unequal sharers; the herald and the headman are equal sharers; the chamberlain and the charioteer are equal sharers."

12.15.109.s: sa yo nu matākṣa iva sa rājña āsana upaviśya catuḥśatam akṣān apacchidyāha | udbhinnam̐ rājñas | iti
12.15.109.d: स यो नु मताक्ष इव स राज्ञ आसन उपविश्य चतुःशतम् अक्षान् अपच्छिद्याह । उद्भिन्नँ राज्ञस् । इति
12.15.109.m: He who is considered skilled at dice, sitting on the king's seat and taking off one hundred and four dice, says: "The king's [throw] has won!"

12.15.109.s: tān eva manāksamantān iva kṛtvāha kṛtaṃ brāhmaṇasya | iti |
12.15.109.d: तान् एव मनाक्समन्तान् इव कृत्वाह कृतं ब्राह्मणस्य । इति ।
12.15.109.m: Making them slightly all-encompassing, as it were, he says: "The winning throw belongs to the brāhmaṇa!"

12.15.109.s: athaitam odanam udbruvate samānām̐śinau brahmā ca yajamānaś ca nānām̐śinau sūtagrāmaṇinau nānām̐śinau kṣattasaṃgrahītārau
12.15.109.d: अथैतम् ओदनम् उद्ब्रुवते समानाँशिनौ ब्रह्मा च यजमानश् च नानाँशिनौ सूतग्रामणिनौ नानाँशिनौ क्षत्तसंग्रहीतारौ
12.15.109.m: Then they announce this rice mess: "The brahman priest and the sacrificer are equal sharers; the herald and the headman are unequal sharers; the chamberlain and the charioteer are unequal sharers."

12.15.109.s: sa yaḥ parājayate tasyainaṃ kule kṣattā pācayati yāvad eṣa odanaḥ pacyate tāvad eṣa hotā śaunaḥśepam ākhyāpayate hiraṇmaye kaśipāv āsīnas
12.15.109.d: स यः पराजयते तस्यैनं कुले क्षत्ता पाचयति यावद् एष ओदनः पच्यते तावद् एष होता शौनःशेपम् आख्यापयते हिरण्मये कशिपाव् आसीनस्
12.15.109.m: Whoever is defeated, in his family the chamberlain cooks this [rice mess]. While this rice mess is being cooked, the hotṛ priest recites the story of Śunaḥśepa, seated on a golden cushion.

12.15.109.s: tasmā adhvaryuḥ pratigṛṇāti hiraṇmaye kūrca āsīnaḥ ||
12.15.109.d: तस्मा अध्वर्युः प्रतिगृणाति हिरण्मये कूर्च आसीनः ॥
12.15.109.m: The adhvaryu priest responds to him, seated on a golden stool:

12.16.109.s: om̐ hotas tathā hotaḥ satyam̐ hotar arātsma hotar iti
12.16.109.d: ओँ होतस् तथा होतः सत्यँ होतर् अरात्स्म होतर् इति
12.16.109.m: "Om, O hotṛ! Yes, O hotṛ! It is true, O hotṛ! We have succeeded, O hotṛ!"

12.16.109.s: yady u vai hotā nādhyety anya u hotrāśam̐sī śam̐sati tasmā u pratiprasthātā pratigṛṇāti
12.16.109.d: यद्य् उ वै होता नाध्येत्य् अन्य उ होत्राशँसी शँसति तस्मा उ प्रतिप्रस्थाता प्रतिगृणाति
12.16.109.m: If indeed the hotṛ priest does not know it, another reciting priest recites; and to him the pratiprasthātṛ priest responds.

12.16.110.m: "There are more than a hundred [verses]," says the brāhmaṇa passage.

12.16.110.s: yadaiṣa odanaḥ pakvo bhavaty athainam ekadhoddhṛtya brahmaṇa upaharati
12.16.110.d: यदैष ओदनः पक्वो भवत्य् अथैनम् एकधोद्धृत्य ब्रह्मण उपहरति
12.16.110.m: When this rice mess is cooked, then, taking it up in a single portion, he brings it near for the brahman priest.

12.16.110.s: tasmā etām̐ś caiva maṇīn dadāti śataṃ vipathaṃ catuṣpātkṣetram atha hotre dadāti śataṃ vipatham̐ hiraṇmayaṃ kaśipu |
12.16.110.d: तस्मा एताँश् चैव मणीन् ददाति शतं विपथं चतुष्पात्क्षेत्रम् अथ होत्रे ददाति शतं विपथँ हिरण्मयं कशिपु ।
12.16.110.m: To him he gives both these jewels, a hundred [cows], a rough wagon, and a field with four-footed beasts. Then he gives to the hotṛ priest a hundred [cows], a rough wagon, and the golden cushion.
Then he gives to the udgātṛ priest a hundred [cows] and a rough wagon.

12.16.110.s: athādhvaryave dadāti śataṃ vipatham̐ svarathaṃ tisraḥ pañcāśataḥ sauvarṇān akṣān hiraṇmayaṃ kūrcam iti |
12.16.110.d: अथाध्वर्यवे ददाति शतं विपथँ स्वरथं तिस्रः पञ्चाशतः सौवर्णान् अक्षान् हिरण्मयं कूर्चम् इति ।
12.16.110.m: Then he gives to the adhvaryu priest a hundred [cows], a rough wagon, his own chariot, the three times fifty golden dice, and the golden stool.

12.16.110.s: atraibhya etan nirjayam̐ sahasraṃ caturdhā kṛtvā dadati |
12.16.110.d: अत्रैभ्य एतन् निर्जयँ सहस्रं चतुर्धा कृत्वा ददति ।
12.16.110.m: Here they divide this won booty of a thousand into four parts and give it to them.

12.16.110.s: athainam etayāsandyā sada āvahantyā vā vrajati |
12.16.110.d: अथैनम् एतयासन्द्या सद आवहन्त्या वा व्रजति ।
12.16.110.m: Then they carry him in this throne-seat to the sadas shed, or he walks [there].

12.16.110.s: anvāyanty enam ete camasās | atraitayor haviṣor iḍām upahvayate |
12.16.110.d: अन्वायन्त्य् एनम् एते चमसास् । अत्रैतयोर् हविषोर् इडाम् उपह्वयते ।
12.16.110.m: These cups follow after him. Here he invokes the iḍā of these two oblations.

12.16.110.s: iḍopahūtaṃ māhendram̐ hotā caivādhvaryuś ca saṃbhakṣayatas |
12.16.110.d: इडोपहूतं माहेन्द्रँ होता चैवाध्वर्युश् च संभक्षयतस् ।
12.16.110.m: The hotṛ priest and the adhvaryu priest consume together the Māhendra cup invoked with the iḍā.

12.16.110.s: narāśam̐sapītena nārāśam̐sān hotṛcamasam evaite trayaḥ samupahūya bhakṣayanti
12.16.110.d: नराशँसपीतेन नाराशँसान् होतृचमसम् एवैते त्रयः समुपहूय भक्षयन्ति
12.16.110.m: They consume the nārāśaṃsa cups with the nārāśaṃsapīta recitation. These three, having invited one another, consume the hotṛ priest's cup;

12.16.110.s: yathācamasaṃ camasān hinva me | ity ātmānaṃ pratyabhimṛśante
12.16.110.d: यथाचमसं चमसान् हिन्व मे । इत्य् आत्मानं प्रत्यभिमृशन्ते
12.16.110.m: [they consume] the cups cup by cup. With "Urge my [limbs]!" they touch themselves.
They do not swell the cups. Having consumed everything, they purify themselves.

12.16.110.s: atha | indrāya tvendrāya tvā | ity evaṃ tribhir ukthyaparyāyaiś carati saṃtiṣṭhate mādhyaṃdinam̐ savanam |
12.16.110.d: अथ । इन्द्राय त्वेन्द्राय त्वा । इत्य् एवं त्रिभिर् उक्थ्यपर्यायैश् चरति संतिष्ठते माध्यंदिनँ सवनम् ।
12.16.110.m: Then, with "To Indra thee, to Indra thee!" in this way he proceeds with three ukthya rounds. The midday pressing is concluded.

12.16.110.s: prasarpanti tṛtīyasavanāya prasiddham ādityagraheṇa caritvāgrayaṇaṃ graḥṇāti |
12.16.110.d: प्रसर्पन्ति तृतीयसवनाय प्रसिद्धम् आदित्यग्रहेण चरित्वाग्रयणं ग्रःणाति ।
12.16.110.m: They crawl forward for the third pressing. Having proceeded with the Āditya cup in the prescribed manner, he draws the āgrayaṇa cup.

12.16.111.m: Then he draws the ukthya cup. The rite is identical up to the pavamāna chant.

12.16.111.s: pavamānena caritvā sve dhāman paśubhyāṃ carati
12.16.111.d: पवमानेन चरित्वा स्वे धामन् पशुभ्यां चरति
12.16.111.m: Having proceeded with the pavamāna chant, he proceeds with the two victims at their own location.

12.16.111.s: tayor nānā manote nānā devate nānā pratyabhimarśanau nānā vasāhomau samāno vanaspatiḥ samānaḥ sviṣṭakṛt praiṣavān samānīḍā samānyo diśas |
12.16.111.d: तयोर् नाना मनोते नाना देवते नाना प्रत्यभिमर्शनौ नाना वसाहोमौ समानो वनस्पतिः समानः स्विष्टकृत् प्रैषवान् समानीडा समान्यो दिशस् ।
12.16.111.m: For the two, there are different manotā hymns, different deities, different touchings, and different omentum libations; the Vanaspati offering is common, the Sviṣṭakṛt offering with orders is common, the iḍā is common, and the quarters are common.

12.16.111.s: nānā diśa ity eke samānaṃ karmāvabhṛthāt | athaitasminn avabhṛtha upādadate cārmapakṣyāv upānahau
12.16.111.d: नाना दिश इत्य् एके समानं कर्मावभृथात् । अथैतस्मिन्न् अवभृथ उपाददते चार्मपक्ष्याव् उपानहौ
12.16.111.m: 'The quarters are different,' say some. The rite is identical up to the purificatory bath. Then at this purificatory bath they put on two leather-flapped shoes.
Having set the boar-skin shoes afloat, he steps out with the two leather-flapped ones.

12.16.111.s: so 'pāmante juhoti | apāṃ naptre svāhā | iti
12.16.111.d: सो ऽपामन्ते जुहोति । अपां नप्त्रे स्वाहा । इति
12.16.111.m: He offers at the edge of the water: "To the Child of the Waters, svāhā!"

12.16.111.s: viṣuvati darbhastambe juhoti | ūrjo naptre svāhā | iti
12.16.111.d: विषुवति दर्भस्तम्बे जुहोति । ऊर्जो नप्त्रे स्वाहा । इति
12.16.111.m: He offers in a clump of darbha grass at the midpoint: "To the Child of Vigour, svāhā!"

12.16.111.s: punaretya gārhapatye juhoti | agnaye gṛhapataye svāhā | iti prasiddho 'vabhṛthas |
12.16.111.d: पुनरेत्य गार्हपत्ये जुहोति । अग्नये गृहपतये स्वाहा । इति प्रसिद्धो ऽवभृथस् ।
12.16.111.m: Returning, he offers in the gārhapatya fire: "To Agni, lord of the house, svāhā!" The purificatory bath is prescribed.

12.16.111.s: udayanīyeṣṭyeṣṭvā maitrāvaruṇīṃ vaśām upākaroti tasyai prasiddhaṃ vapayā caritvā naiva śmaśrūṇi vapate na keśān
12.16.111.d: उदयनीयेष्ट्येष्ट्वा मैत्रावरुणीं वशाम् उपाकरोति तस्यै प्रसिद्धं वपया चरित्वा नैव श्मश्रूणि वपते न केशान्
12.16.111.m: Having performed the concluding sacrifice, he dedicates a barren cow to Mitra and Varuṇa. Having proceeded with its omentum in the prescribed manner, he shaves neither beard nor hair.
